# S.E.E. Official Library

> Every authoring guide and schema page for the S.E.E. Official Library, combined into one file. It covers how to write workflows, prompts, skills, commands, bundles, and cycles, how to publish them to the catalog, and the hub document schemas the runtime validates on save.

The Official Library is the package catalog that S.E.E. installs from. A package
is a versioned payload plus an install map, so machinery written in one project
can be used in another.

Two things are authoritative and machine readable:

- `catalog.json` (https://garunski.github.io/s_e_e_library/catalog.json) lists
  every package and where each file installs. Its schema tag is `see.library/v1` or `see.library/v2`.
- The JSON Schema files under
  https://garunski.github.io/s_e_e_library/schema/ define each payload shape.

Each section below mirrors one page on
https://garunski.github.io/s_e_e_library/ and names it on a `Source:` line, in
site order: how to author each package type first, then the payload contracts.
Where a section and a schema file disagree, the schema file wins.

Story authors: see **Story authoring packages** in the Skills section for the
mandatory specificity review. It applies before a story is handed off,
scheduled, or moved into active work and whenever its scope changes.
Milestone authors: see **Milestone authoring packages** in the Skills section
for the cut, membership, and completion review.

## Contents

# Authoring overview

Source: /authoring/

Project settings > Experimental controls project-local runtime availability. All six switches default to off. Package storage and reusable workflows remain available. MCP discovery across authorized projects can expose a tool enabled elsewhere, while every invocation checks its target project. See [Experimental configuration and API contract](/schema/hub-config/) and [Research profiles, availability and MCP examples](/schema/knowledge-research/).

Every package in the Official Library is one of six types. Pick the type, write
its payload, then publish it to the catalog.

## Package types

- [Workflows](/authoring/workflows/): task graphs the engine runs (`definition.json`)
- [Prompts](/authoring/prompts/): named instruction text (`prompt.json`)
- [Skills](/authoring/skills/): activatable capability guides (`SKILL.md`)
- [Commands](/authoring/commands/): worker definitions for an agent CLI (`command.json`)
- [Bundles](/authoring/bundles/): install maps that deliver several packages together
- [Cycles](/authoring/cycles/): host loops wiring workflows to stores (`cycle.json`)

## Publishing

- [Publish to the catalog](/authoring/publish/): payload layout, the `catalog.json` entry, and validation

## Schema reference

- Catalog manifest: [`see.library/v1`](/catalog.json)
- Payload contract, per-type schemas, and hub document schemas: [S.E.E. schemas](/schema/)
- Research HTTP/MCP wire contract and profile versions: [Research schema](/schema/knowledge-research/)

## Knowledge Research schema

Source: /schema/knowledge-research/

The S.E.E. Research wire contract exposes 28 scoped HTTP and MCP operations for research, report, analysis and guide. Runtime profile descriptors are version 1; knowledge_research_profile_get defines their required roles and rules.

## Availability and discovery

Enable knowledge_research in Project settings > Experimental for the explicit target project. It defaults to false. Disabling preserves documents, pages and immutable editions while omitting Research views, shared search hits, exact-project resources and qualified prompts. Calls return EXPERIMENTAL_FEATURE_DISABLED. Ordinary knowledge docs and decisions remain available. Mixed-project discovery can advertise tools enabled elsewhere; invocation still checks the explicit target project. Start with knowledge_research_profile_get and knowledge_research_list.

## Payload boundaries and selectors

Document and page get return metadata, counts and document_token or page_token only. Section get and source get return one complete record and section_token or source_token. Document/page metadata reject nested child bodies. Creation allocates research_id; stable child keys are create-if-absent. Mutation responses contain affected records and tokens, with bounded diagnostics; membership changes also return the changed parent token. All request and response schemas are defined in the machine schema, including the structured error envelope.

Document and page manifests, independent section/source files and immutable edition directories are the storage boundaries. Ordinary reads and writes never reconstruct a full ResearchDocument or ResearchWorkingCopy. Use section_put with section_token, source_put with source_token, document put with document_token and page put with page_token. Page create/pages_reorder require document_token; section create/sections_reorder require page_token. Page delete requires page_token and document_token; section delete requires section_token and page_token. Deletions require confirm=true. Publish and whole-document delete use tree_token from current validation. Source create needs no parent token. A stale token requires rereading and reconciling only the affected record.

Lists default to 25, accept 1..100 and return items, next_cursor and limit. The document catalogue retains the shared typed metadata filters envelope, discovered using list_filter_get for knowledge_research: filters compose with kind, tag, query and state using AND before pagination. MCP sends a predicate array; HTTP/resource queries encode the JSON array once as filters. See collection-filter.schema.json. Catalogue state=all|draft|published is distinct from content view=default|draft|edition. Default reads resolve the latest edition or unpublished draft; view=edition requires edition_id, rejected for other views. Pin the resolved view/edition and normalized filter selection while following opaque continuations; restart invalid/stale cursors. Protocol tools/list cursors are independent.

Search uses knowledge_research_search and GET /api/projects/{project}/knowledge/research/search. Query is required, 1..256 Unicode characters, with AND terms and no regex. Filters include research_id, page_key, kind, role, tag, view and edition_id; edition_id requires research_id. Hits carry section identities and snippets at most 240 characters, never full bodies. Edition metadata uses edition_list/edition_get; exact-edition page/section/source reads use view=edition and edition_id. Resource reads never mutate or fetch external sources.

## Errors and publication

The scoped error envelope has code, affected_ids, field_path, remedy and optional current_token. HTTP 400: invalid_key, invalid_order, invalid_filter, invalid_cursor, stale_cursor, unknown_fields, missing_token. HTTP 404: not_found, view_not_found. HTTP 409: stale_token, already_exists, referenced_source, nonempty_page, tree_changed. HTTP 422: invalid_content, invalid_publication. Project/auth admission errors retain existing semantics without foreign identity disclosure, including MISSING_PROJECT, PROJECT_NOT_GRANTED and EXPERIMENTAL_FEATURE_DISABLED. Applicable operation errors are listed on the authoring page and in x-operations.

Follow every validate diagnostics page, repair affected records and revalidate. Publication recomputes and validates the exact tree before creating an immutable separate-files edition. Publish only when requested. Small-page guidance (3-8 sections and about 1500 words) is advisory; preserve supplied long content without truncation, summarization or automatic splitting.

Machine schema: [knowledge-research.schema.json](/schema/knowledge-research.schema.json).

## Research authoring

Source: /authoring/research/

Research in S.E.E. supports research, reports, analysis and guides through 28 scoped operations.

## Project availability

Enable `knowledge_research` in Project settings > Experimental for the explicit target project. It defaults to false independently of Knowledge Cycle and Orchestrator. Disabling preserves documents, pages and immutable editions while omitting Research views, shared search hits, exact-project resources and qualified Research prompts. Subsequent HTTP and MCP operations return `EXPERIMENTAL_FEATURE_DISABLED`. Ordinary knowledge docs and decisions remain available. Mixed-project MCP discovery may advertise tools enabled in another authorized project; invocation still checks the explicit target project.

Discover `knowledge_research_profile_get` and the current tool schemas before authoring. The four runtime profile descriptors are version 1 and define required roles and field rules. Use the qualified `{project}.research-authoring` prompt for the producer procedure.

## Separate files and bounded reads

Under Knowledge/research/{research_id}/, `manifest.json` stores document metadata and ordered page_keys. Each `pages/{page_key}/manifest.json` stores page metadata and ordered section_keys. Section Markdown lives independently in `pages/{page_key}/sections/{section_key}.json`; bibliography records live in `sources/{source_id}.json`. Immutable editions use this same separate-file layout under `editions/{edition_id}/`. Internal .locks and .transactions are excluded from lists and search. Never send a full ResearchDocument or ResearchWorkingCopy to edit one scope.

Document get returns metadata, counts and document_token; page get returns metadata, section count and page_token. Neither read returns child bodies or embedded sources. Lists return summaries, stable identities, positions where relevant, limit and next_cursor. Section get returns exactly one complete section and section_token; source get returns exactly one complete source and source_token.

Lists default to 25 and accept 1..100. Keep filters and the resolved view unchanged while following opaque next_cursor or resource continuation URIs; restart after invalid_cursor or stale_cursor. Content view=default resolves the latest published edition or draft when unpublished. Use view=draft for edits; view=edition requires edition_id, which is rejected for other views. Pin the resolved edition across navigation and continuations. Catalogue state=all|draft|published is independent of content view: draft means never published.

Use list_filter_get for knowledge_research to discover the retained typed metadata predicate envelope: `filters: [{field, op, value}]`. It composes with kind, tag, query and state using AND before pagination. Keep the normalized predicates and selectors unchanged across cursors. HTTP and resource queries encode the predicate array once as JSON in filters; MCP sends the array directly. This is the shared collection-filter language, not a new Research filter DSL. Scoped list responses use items, next_cursor and limit.

Research has its own `knowledge_research_search` and GET /api/projects/{project}/knowledge/research/search endpoint. Query is required, at most 256 Unicode characters, with case-insensitive AND matching of whitespace-separated terms and no regex. Filters are research_id, page_key, kind, role, tag, view and edition_id; edition_id also requires research_id. Hits contain section identities and snippets of at most 240 Unicode characters, never complete bodies. Search defaults to 25, maximum 100. Resource reads never mutate, publish or fetch external sources.

## Authoring and token scopes

Search before creating duplicate material. Plan one coherent topic per page, normally 3-8 sections and roughly 1500 words or fewer. These are advisory warnings. Preserve supplied substantive Markdown, tables, code, citations and long content exactly: do not truncate, summarize or automatically split content to satisfy the guidance. Required profile roles may span pages; keep stable lowercase ASCII letter/digit/hyphen keys when titles change.

Create document metadata only and use the allocated research_id. Create page metadata separately with the current document_token. Create each section separately with the current page_token. Create sources independently before referencing their stable source_ids. Create is create-if-absent; put updates existing records only. Metadata endpoints reject nested child bodies.

| Action | Latest required token fields |
| --- | --- |
| Document settings put | document_token from document get |
| Page create or pages_reorder | document_token |
| Page details put | page_token from page get |
| Empty page delete | page_token and document_token, confirm=true |
| Section create or sections_reorder | page_token |
| Section put | section_token from section get |
| Section delete | section_token and page_token, confirm=true |
| Source create | none; stable create-if-absent source_id |
| Source put or delete | source_token from source get; delete also confirm=true |
| Publish or whole-document delete | tree_token from current validation; delete also confirm=true |

Do not send generic conflict_token to scoped Research operations. Reorder requests contain every current child key exactly once. Page/section membership changes return the affected record and changed parent token. Source creation does not rewrite the document manifest. Nonempty pages and referenced sources cannot be deleted; deletion never cascades.

Read the selected draft section, save exactly that section with section_put and its current section_token, then read back exact Markdown, source IDs, evidence and resulting token. Save document settings, page details and sources independently with their own puts and tokens. On stale_token, reread and reconcile only the affected scope, preserve intervening and unrelated content, then retry with that record's current token. A tree token is never required for an ordinary section edit.

Keep source access truth: inspected, provided, metadata_only or unavailable, with locator, inspected scope and limitations. Never invent inspection claims, measurements or successful procedures. Source-backed sections name existing source IDs; distinguish author_reasoning, illustrative and not_applicable evidence. Reports require reporting context and typed actions with owner/unassigned ownership and due date/condition.

Run knowledge_research_validate, follow every diagnostics page tied to the tree token and repair only affected records at their field paths. If the tree changes during pagination, restart validation. Revalidate after repairs. Structural validation does not prove source truth or argument quality. Publish only when requested, using the current validated tree_token. Publication recomputes and validates the exact tree and creates an immutable edition; Draft save is not publication. Read edition metadata with edition_get and selected content with view=edition and the returned edition_id. Report affected IDs, exact saved readback, remaining diagnostics and Draft or edition state.

## Errors

Scoped errors contain code, affected_ids, field_path and remedy, plus current_token when disclosure is allowed. HTTP uses 400 for invalid_key, invalid_order, invalid_filter, invalid_cursor, stale_cursor, unknown_fields and missing_token; 404 for not_found and view_not_found; 409 for stale_token, already_exists, referenced_source, nonempty_page and tree_changed; 422 for invalid_content and invalid_publication. Authentication and project-grant errors retain existing semantics without foreign identity disclosure. MISSING_PROJECT, PROJECT_NOT_GRANTED and EXPERIMENTAL_FEATURE_DISABLED remain admission errors.

Correct malformed fields or order, restart stale cursors, reread only the affected record for token conflicts, choose an unused identity for duplicate creates, remove references explicitly before deleting a source, and empty a page explicitly before deleting it. A tree_changed publication requires current validation again. Do not publish as automatic conflict or diagnostic repair.

| Operation | HTTP | Path | Scope | Applicable scoped errors |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| knowledge_research_profile_get | GET | /api/projects/{project}/knowledge/research/profiles/{kind} | Versioned profile descriptor | invalid_key, unknown_fields, not_found |
| knowledge_research_list | GET | /api/projects/{project}/knowledge/research/ | Document summaries only; kind,tag,query,state filters | invalid_key, unknown_fields, invalid_cursor, stale_cursor, invalid_filter |
| knowledge_research_get | GET | /api/projects/{project}/knowledge/research/{id} | Document metadata and counts only | invalid_key, unknown_fields, not_found, view_not_found |
| knowledge_research_create | POST | /api/projects/{project}/knowledge/research/ | Metadata only; allocate id | invalid_key, unknown_fields, invalid_content |
| knowledge_research_put | PUT | /api/projects/{project}/knowledge/research/{id} | Metadata only with document token | invalid_key, unknown_fields, not_found, missing_token, stale_token, invalid_content |
| knowledge_research_delete | DELETE | /api/projects/{project}/knowledge/research/{id} | Explicit confirm and current tree token; delete exact document | invalid_key, unknown_fields, not_found, missing_token, stale_token, tree_changed |
| knowledge_research_page_list | GET | /api/projects/{project}/knowledge/research/{id}/pages | Page summaries; query filter and explicit positions | invalid_key, unknown_fields, not_found, invalid_cursor, stale_cursor, invalid_filter, view_not_found |
| knowledge_research_page_get | GET | /api/projects/{project}/knowledge/research/{id}/pages/{page} | Page metadata and section count only | invalid_key, unknown_fields, not_found, view_not_found |
| knowledge_research_page_create | POST | /api/projects/{project}/knowledge/research/{id}/pages | Create metadata and append key atomically; document token | invalid_key, unknown_fields, not_found, missing_token, stale_token, already_exists, invalid_content |
| knowledge_research_page_put | PUT | /api/projects/{project}/knowledge/research/{id}/pages/{page} | Page metadata only; page token | invalid_key, unknown_fields, not_found, missing_token, stale_token, invalid_content |
| knowledge_research_page_delete | DELETE | /api/projects/{project}/knowledge/research/{id}/pages/{page} | Empty page only; page and document tokens; no cascading deletion | invalid_key, unknown_fields, not_found, missing_token, stale_token, nonempty_page, invalid_content |
| knowledge_research_pages_reorder | PUT | /api/projects/{project}/knowledge/research/{id}/page-order | Exact ordered page keys; document token | invalid_key, unknown_fields, not_found, missing_token, stale_token, invalid_order |
| knowledge_research_section_list | GET | /api/projects/{project}/knowledge/research/{id}/pages/{page}/sections | Section summaries; role,query filters and explicit positions | invalid_key, unknown_fields, not_found, invalid_cursor, stale_cursor, invalid_filter, view_not_found |
| knowledge_research_section_get | GET | /api/projects/{project}/knowledge/research/{id}/pages/{page}/sections/{section} | Exactly one section with Markdown, evidence and section token | invalid_key, unknown_fields, not_found, view_not_found |
| knowledge_research_section_create | POST | /api/projects/{project}/knowledge/research/{id}/pages/{page}/sections | One section and append key atomically; page token | invalid_key, unknown_fields, not_found, missing_token, stale_token, already_exists, invalid_content |
| knowledge_research_section_put | PUT | /api/projects/{project}/knowledge/research/{id}/pages/{page}/sections/{section} | Exactly one section; section token | invalid_key, unknown_fields, not_found, missing_token, stale_token, invalid_content |
| knowledge_research_section_delete | DELETE | /api/projects/{project}/knowledge/research/{id}/pages/{page}/sections/{section} | Explicit confirm; section and page tokens | invalid_key, unknown_fields, not_found, missing_token, stale_token, invalid_content |
| knowledge_research_sections_reorder | PUT | /api/projects/{project}/knowledge/research/{id}/pages/{page}/section-order | Exact section keys; page token | invalid_key, unknown_fields, not_found, missing_token, stale_token, invalid_order |
| knowledge_research_source_list | GET | /api/projects/{project}/knowledge/research/{id}/sources | Source summaries; query,access_status,locator_kind filters | invalid_key, unknown_fields, not_found, invalid_cursor, stale_cursor, invalid_filter, view_not_found |
| knowledge_research_source_get | GET | /api/projects/{project}/knowledge/research/{id}/sources/{source} | Exactly one source record and source token | invalid_key, unknown_fields, not_found, view_not_found |
| knowledge_research_source_create | POST | /api/projects/{project}/knowledge/research/{id}/sources | One source; create-if-absent stable source_id | invalid_key, unknown_fields, not_found, already_exists, invalid_content |
| knowledge_research_source_put | PUT | /api/projects/{project}/knowledge/research/{id}/sources/{source} | Exactly one source; source token | invalid_key, unknown_fields, not_found, missing_token, stale_token, invalid_content |
| knowledge_research_source_delete | DELETE | /api/projects/{project}/knowledge/research/{id}/sources/{source} | Confirm and source token; reject if referenced | invalid_key, unknown_fields, not_found, missing_token, stale_token, referenced_source, invalid_content |
| knowledge_research_search | GET | /api/projects/{project}/knowledge/research/search | Bounded section hits; document,page,kind,role,tag,view,edition filters | invalid_key, unknown_fields, invalid_cursor, stale_cursor, invalid_filter, view_not_found |
| knowledge_research_validate | POST | /api/projects/{project}/knowledge/research/{id}/validate | Consistent complete-tree validation; paged diagnostics and tree token | invalid_key, unknown_fields, not_found, invalid_cursor, stale_cursor, tree_changed, invalid_content |
| knowledge_research_publish | POST | /api/projects/{project}/knowledge/research/{id}/publish | Current validated tree token; immutable separate-files edition | invalid_key, unknown_fields, not_found, missing_token, stale_token, tree_changed, invalid_publication |
| knowledge_research_edition_list | GET | /api/projects/{project}/knowledge/research/{id}/editions | Edition summaries only | invalid_key, unknown_fields, not_found, invalid_cursor, stale_cursor, invalid_filter |
| knowledge_research_edition_get | GET | /api/projects/{project}/knowledge/research/{id}/editions/{edition} | Edition metadata and counts only | invalid_key, unknown_fields, not_found, view_not_found |

### Four-kind request sequences

```json
[
  {
    "kind": "research",
    "instructions": "Illustrative Draft sequence; substitute allocated IDs and FROM_* markers from the latest reads. Cover all profile roles before validation/publication; publish only on request.",
    "calls": [
      {
        "tool": "knowledge_research_profile_get",
        "arguments": {
          "project": "example",
          "kind": "research"
        }
      },
      {
        "tool": "knowledge_research_search",
        "arguments": {
          "project": "example",
          "query": "topic",
          "view": "draft",
          "limit": 25
        }
      },
      {
        "tool": "knowledge_research_list",
        "arguments": {
          "project": "example",
          "state": "draft",
          "filters": [
            {
              "field": "title",
              "op": "contains",
              "value": "topic"
            }
          ],
          "limit": 25
        }
      },
      {
        "tool": "knowledge_research_create",
        "arguments": {
          "project": "example",
          "document": {
            "kind": "research",
            "profile_version": 1,
            "title": "Topic research",
            "audience": "Maintainers",
            "purpose": "Explain the bounded topic",
            "key_message": "Illustrative draft",
            "scope": "One topic",
            "basis": "Supplied notes",
            "tags": [
              "example"
            ]
          }
        }
      },
      {
        "tool": "knowledge_research_get",
        "arguments": {
          "project": "example",
          "research_id": "research-1",
          "view": "draft"
        }
      },
      {
        "tool": "knowledge_research_page_create",
        "arguments": {
          "project": "example",
          "research_id": "research-1",
          "document_token": "FROM_DOCUMENT_GET",
          "page": {
            "page_key": "topic",
            "title": "Topic",
            "summary": "One coherent topic"
          }
        }

          "view": "draft"
        }
      },

          "project": "example",
          "research_id": "research-1",
          "source_id": "provided-notes",
          "source_token": "FROM_SOURCE_GET",
          "source": {
            "source_id": "provided-notes",
            "title": "Provided notes",
            "locator_kind": "file",
            "locator": "operator-supplied-notes",
            "access_status": "provided",
            "inspected_scope": "Only supplied excerpt",
            "limitation": "Original source not inspected"
          }
        }
      },
      {
        "tool": "knowledge_research_section_create",
        "arguments": {
          "project": "example",
          "research_id": "research-1",
          "page_key": "topic",
          "page_token": "FROM_PAGE_GET",
          "section": {
            "section_key": "context",
            "role": "context",
            "heading": "Context",
            "content": "Illustrative supplied Markdown.\n\n```text\nKeep exact content.\n```\n",
            "source_ids": [
              "provided-notes"
            ],
            "evidence_basis": "source_backed",
            "evidence_note": "Supplied excerpt only",
            "action_items": []
          }
        }
      },
      {
        "tool": "knowledge_research_section_get",
        "arguments": {
          "project": "example",
          "research_id": "research-1",
          "page_key": "topic",
          "section_key": "context",
          "view": "draft"
        }
      },
      {
        "tool": "knowledge_research_section_put",
        "arguments": {
          "project": "example",
          "research_id": "research-1",
          "page_key": "topic",
          "section_key": "context",
          "section_token": "FROM_SECTION_GET",
          "section": {
            "section_key": "context",
            "role": "context",
            "heading": "Context",

  {
    "kind": "report",

            "title": "Topic",
            "summary": "One coherent topic"

        }

        "tool": "knowledge_research_page_get",
        "arguments": {
          "project": "example",
          "research_id": "research-1",
          "page_key": "topic",
          "view": "draft"
```

---

# Workflows

Source: /authoring/workflows/

## Definition homes

The home labels are This machine and Project: Example.

This machine contains definitions for the current OS user.

Machine definitions are stored under ~/.s_e_e/definitions/.

Workflow runs, logs, schedules, cycles, and execution history remain per project.

Machine definitions are outside project Git and project backups; back up ~/.s_e_e/definitions/ separately.

A machine workflow runs only after a target project is selected.

Prompts, commands and workflow definitions can live in either home. Duplicate ids and names remain distinct; neither home shadows the other. `machine:review` selects the machine definition; `project:review` selects the target project's definition. A bare `review` remains project-only. Prompt templates use `{{prompt.machine:review}}` or `{{prompt.project:review}}`; legacy `{{prompt.review}}` stays project-only. Missing or incompatible selections stay flagged for repair and are never replaced by the same id in another home.

Machine workflows must omit `spoke_root` everywhere in their content and cannot depend on project-only prompts or commands. Their working context comes from the selected project at launch. Project workflows may use either home. Schedules, cycle stages and project defaults store explicit references but keep their project owner. A run captures definition content, exact home and revision; later edits or deletion do not rewrite that snapshot. Legacy runs with no captured provenance remain unknown.

Definition search retains exact home, kind, path and editor destination for duplicate names. Machine-only search works without selecting a project and exposes only authorized prompt, command and workflow metadata, never project business data. HTTP uses `/api/machine/definitions/search`; selected-project search stays under `/api/projects/{code}/search`. Denied machine access and unauthorized projects do not expose titles, snippets or counts. Reopening search refreshes definition revisions.

Copy previews identify the source, destination, concrete paths and dependency rewrites. Review renamed dependencies and explicit reuse before applying the preview token. Copying leaves the original and existing bindings intact. Editing a machine definition affects future uses across projects. Deletion checks project usage; stale or inaccessible usage blocks deletion. Existing runs retain captured content.

Client grants separate project access from machine definition read/edit permissions. Machine access defaults off; edit implies read. A project-only worker token cannot edit machine definitions. Machine prompt discovery requires machine read and an explicit authorized target project for expansion; project access alone does not grant machine access.

The workflow guide examples use one machine workflow with two different explicit project targets in `workflow_execute` arguments. They illustrate request structure; execution ownership is verified separately. No machine execution endpoint is introduced.

### Machine workflow and launch arguments

Stored definition (no spoke_root):

```json
{
  "id": "review",
  "name": "Review",
  "version": 1,
  "is_edited": false,
  "created_at": "2026-11-07T00:00:00Z",
  "updated_at": "2026-11-07T00:00:00Z",
  "content": {
    "id": "review",
    "name": "Review",
    "tasks": [{"id": "inspect", "name": "Inspect", "function": {"name": "cli_command", "input": {"command": "git", "args": ["status", "--short"]}}}]
  }
}
```

workflow_execute for project-a:

```json
{"project":"project-a","workflow_id":"machine:review","runtime_inputs":{}}
```

workflow_execute for project-b:

```json
{"project":"project-b","workflow_id":"machine:review","runtime_inputs":{}}
```

See [prompt details](/s_e_e_library/authoring/prompts/), [command details](/s_e_e_library/authoring/commands/) and [Library destinations](/s_e_e_library/authoring/bundles/).

## Native collection selection

### Discovery and scope

Call `list_filter_get` with `project` and `collection` before constructing a query. Collections include `stories`, `milestones`, and `knowledge_docs`. The returned descriptor supplies scope, field names, scalar/array types, operators, nullability, and enum choices. Story and milestone status choices come from the project configuration. HTTP discovery uses `GET /api/projects/{project}/list-filters/{collection}`. Application collections use `GET /api/list-filters/{collection}` under application authorization. Discover each collection through its existing authorized surface.

All predicates combine with AND. `in` supplies alternatives for one scalar field. Legacy parameters compose with predicates using AND, so contradictory selections return no rows. Authorization and mandatory scopes, including active-draft, compatible-only and running-only constraints, still apply. Fields are public metadata declared by the descriptor. Body text, secrets and arbitrary JSON paths are unavailable.

### Encoding and operators

Native tools, MCP and workflow tool inputs take a typed `filters` array. HTTP GET uses one URL-encoded JSON array in the `filters` query parameter. For example, `curl --get --data-urlencode 'filters=[{"field":"status","op":"ne","value":"Done"}]' 'http://127.0.0.1:30127/api/projects/s-e-e/stories?milestone=m-45'` encodes a story selection. Native `story_list` calls name the legacy selector `milestone_id`; the HTTP query and Rust `StoryListRequest` name it `milestone`. The descriptor field is `milestone_id` on every surface. The Rust client's `*_with_filters` methods perform the encoding and retain predicates across pages. Resource query templates are advertised by `resources/templates/list` for existing entity resources.

- `eq`, `ne`, `in`, and `not_in` compare same-type scalars. Identifier and enum equality is case sensitive.
- `contains` is a case-insensitive substring on a declared string field, using Unicode lowercase without accent folding.
- `contains_any`, `contains_all`, and `contains_none` compare array membership.
- `gte` and `lte` compare numbers, dates (`YYYY-MM-DD`) or timestamps (RFC3339 with an offset, normalized to UTC).
- `is_set` and `is_unset` omit `value` entirely and are offered only where declared. Missing/null fields fail ordinary predicates, including `ne` and `not_in`. Empty strings and arrays are present values. Null comparison operands are rejected.

Use at most 16 predicates, 100 members per nonempty membership array, 1024 Unicode characters per string operand, and 16384 UTF-8 bytes of decoded filter JSON. Request errors such as malformed JSON, duplicate `filters`, non-array input, or exceeded request bounds have a request-level code and remedy. Predicate diagnostics identify a zero-based `predicate_index`, field, code, and remedy. Correct `unknown_field` from discovery, replace an `invalid_enum` with a descriptor choice, and omit `value` for presence checks. Unsupported operators, wrong types, empty membership arrays and invalid dates are errors.

### Pages, cursors and GUI controls

Selection precedes existing ordering, matching totals and page slicing. Standard offset pages retain `items`, `total`, `offset`, `limit`, and `has_more`, with default limit 50 and maximum 200. Keep predicates on subsequent pages. Other existing responses can be unpaged or omit totals. Use their actual response contract. Native `story_list` traverses matching pages and its text JSON exposes `story_ids` in exactly item order. Pass those IDs directly to `foreach`.

The Board endpoint `GET /api/projects/{project}/stories/columns` applies `limit` and `offset` per status and returns the full matching `stories_total` per status. With `group_by_milestone=true`, paging applies per milestone within each status and `milestone_totals` reports matching counts keyed by milestone ID. The empty key represents unassigned work.

Scoped Research returns `items`, `next_cursor`, and `limit`. Its retained typed filters compose with `kind`, `tag`, `query` and catalogue `state` using AND before pagination. Its cursor is bound to that normalized selection. Keep the selection unchanged while following `next_cursor` and discard the cursor when it changes. Content `view` is separate from catalogue `state`. Protocol catalog cursors from `tools/list`, `prompts/list`, and `resources/list` are separate from entity cursors.

Existing GUI field controls use the same descriptors alongside quick filters. Choose a field and operator, enter a typed value or select enum choices, and remove individual predicates or clear the selection. Changes reset paging/cursors and persist in the URL. Lists distinguish no matching rows from load or access errors. Collection-specific eligibility and saved configuration remain in force.

### Milestone workflow release

The current `work-milestone-stories` bundle release is 1.1.0. Its `system-work-milestone-stories` resolver sends `milestone_id` plus `status ne Done` to native `story_list` and consumes `story_ids` directly. Saved Done/all-checked verification, bounded repair attempts, explicit blockers and one final repository check remain part of the workflow. The final check runs a stored command and uses its exit status.

Review the normal Library upgrade plan. Unmodified defaults can upgrade through that plan. Customized files remain conflicts until an explicit overwrite is chosen. Preserve custom selection and worker instructions when reconciling an upgrade. Historical releases remain available.

### Unfinished milestone stories

Arguments for `story_list`. Substitute your project and milestone IDs and configured status choices.

```json
{
  "project": "s-e-e",
  "milestone_id": "m-45",
  "filters": [
    { "field": "status", "op": "ne", "value": "Done" }
  ]
}
```

### Milestone progress

Arguments for `milestone_list`. Derived progress still describes all member stories.

```json
{
  "project": "s-e-e",
  "filters": [
    { "field": "linked_story_count", "op": "gte", "value": 1 },
    { "field": "completion_percent", "op": "lte", "value": 75 }
  ]
}
```

### Document type and tags

Arguments for `knowledge_doc_list`. Discover `knowledge_docs` for supported type choices.

```json
{
  "project": "s-e-e",
  "filters": [
    { "field": "type", "op": "eq", "value": "specification" },
    { "field": "tags", "op": "contains_all", "value": ["api", "filters"] }
  ]
}
```

### Rejected resource limit

```json
{
  "error": "resource_limit_exceeded: foreach_items allowed 10000, attempted 10001, task items, execution 11111111-1111-4111-8111-111111111111"
```

## Execution runtime and controls

Definitions retain their nested authoring form. Execution uses a flat graph of task IDs and materializes one foreach iteration and one repair attempt at a time. A loop's `wait_for` barrier completes only after the whole loop, including its verifiers, succeeds. An empty successful loop contributes zero action records.

Each run has a supervised worker process. The parent API owns durable execution writes and terminal status. Worker signal exits, nonzero exits, missing terminal exchange and malformed IPC produce a failed run with `worker_aborted` or `worker_protocol_error`. The saved worker failure includes the exit code or signal and a bounded stderr tail. The API and other isolated runs can continue after a worker abort. Host-wide failures can still affect the parent and workers; machine-wide fault isolation is not guaranteed.

**Pause** records a request immediately, stops new admissions and waits for already active steps. The run becomes **Paused** after those steps settle and the checkpoint is saved. Repeated pause requests are idempotent. **Cancel** stops the run and terminates its owned worker and command descendants, with a two-second grace before forced cleanup. Parent disconnect and server shutdown also clean up owned workers and descendants. A control timeout or closed pipe is recorded as cancellation or worker failure, never as a successful pause acknowledgment.

**Resume** continues a safely checkpointed paused run without replaying completed task IDs or losing their outputs. Current checkpoints contain flat graph state, loop cursors, outputs, allocation counters, resource policy and frozen run provenance. Unknown in-flight actions after an interruption are recorded as failures and are not automatically replayed. Reconcile uncertain external side effects before starting replacement work. Exactly-once external effects are not guaranteed. The engine reads the current flat checkpoint format only.

## Progress fields

HTTP execution reads and MCP `execution_get` expose the same `runtime_progress` object. `status` remains authoritative; successful worker startup does not mean Complete.

| Field | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `materialized_tasks`, `completed_tasks` | Actual action IDs currently materialized and completed; templates and loop control barriers are excluded |
| `total_tasks` | `null` while future loop work remains unknown; consumers must omit a percentage instead of showing 100 percent from current materialization |
| `generated_nodes`, `generated_edges` | Lifetime allocations, retained across resume |
| `retained_nodes`, `retained_edges` | Current retained graph size, including templates and controls |
| `loops[].collection_size` | Known foreach collection size, or `null` until its producer resolves |
| `loops[].current_iteration` | Zero-based active foreach index, or `null` |
| `loops[].completed_iterations` | Successfully completed foreach iterations; after item zero of 39 this is 1 of 39 and the barrier is pending |
| `loops[].active_attempt` | One-based active repair attempt, or `null` |
| `loops[].barrier_pending` | Whether the complete loop barrier is still pending |
| `pause_requested` | A request is pending; this differs from a committed Paused state |
| `worker_pid`, `worker_failure` | Owned worker identity and bounded failure diagnostics, when available |

## Resource limits

The policy is selected at launch and preserved on resume. Limits are checked before graph mutation or semantic output retention. A rejected semantic result is not silently truncated into apparently valid task output.

| Limit name | Default |
| --- | --- |
| `authored_bytes` | 8 MiB |
| `authored_depth` | 64 |
| `generated_nodes` | 100,000 over the run's lifetime |
| `generated_edges` | 200,000 over the run's lifetime |
| `foreach_items` | 10,000 per collection |
| `active_handlers` | 32 |
| `task_result_bytes` | 1 MiB encoded structured result |
| `retained_result_bytes` | 64 MiB aggregate retained results |
| `checkpoint_bytes` | 128 MiB encoded checkpoint |

`resource_limit_exceeded` identifies the limit, allowed amount, attempted amount, task ID and execution ID. An HTTP request rejected before acceptance uses the `{error, code?}` envelope. An accepted run reports finite failure details in `errors`; worker failures also use `runtime_progress.worker_failure`. Retained prior outputs and completed evidence remain available after a limit failure.

Worker IPC has a 1 MiB frame body, a 64-frame bounded queue and a 128 MiB total chunked-checkpoint limit. Worker stderr retention uses three 5 MiB files and a 64 KiB diagnostic tail, with dropped-byte accounting. Diagnostic tails may omit bytes; semantic captured JSON must remain complete or fail.

Published response schemas: workflow-execution.schema.json and execution-error.schema.json.


A **workflow** package defines tasks the S.E.E. engine runs against a hub or
spoke. Payload file: `definition.json`. Installs to
`.s_e_e/workflows/definitions/{slug}.json`.

Authoring rules live in the bundled **workflow** skill
(`packages/workflow/1.0.0/SKILL.md`). This page covers the library payload
shape only.

## Envelope (`definition.json`)

| Field | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `id` | Outer id, usually `system-<name>` |
| `name`, `description` | Hub display metadata |
| `content` | Engine workflow object |

## Inner `content`

| Field | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `runtime_inputs` | Run-start values; each object with `key`, `input_type`, `required`, `label`; keys must not contain dots |
| `default_command_id` | Optional installed command id for `command` tasks that omit `command_id` |
| `tasks` | Ordered graph of engine tasks |
| `spoke_root` | Optional. Omit it in Library packages: the run then uses the project's code folder for story implementation and code knowledge workflows, and the project home folder for every other workflow. To let the user pick the folder, set it to an exact `{{runtime.KEY}}` reference to a string runtime input; the run resolves and validates the absolute path before execution and again on resume. Catalog validation rejects a package that sets a literal path. |

### Task types

Each task has exactly one handler under `function`:

- `cli_command`: shell command and args
- `command`: run an installed command definition; omit `command_id` for an unbound task, set workflow `default_command_id`, or pin a non-empty `command_id` to fix the task; optional `prompt` when the definition uses prompt delivery
- `user_input`: pause the run to collect an operator answer when this task is reached
- `git_action`, `s_e_e_action`, `foreach`, `custom`

`s_e_e_action` calls one MCP tool. `input.tool` is the precise named tool id. `item_call` remains for a call that has no named tool. `input.arguments` is that tool's argument object and includes an explicit `project` such as `{{project.id}}`. Tool names are in the Tools reference.

`foreach` has exactly one `next_tasks` entry, and that body must be one chain with a single leaf. A later branch is rejected. Nested `foreach` is allowed when each body is still one chain. A `repair_loop` can be the foreach body: its worker and verifier form one logical chain. Each item keeps its runtime values, attempt outputs and verifier feedback; the next item waits for verification to pass. Its retry budget starts at the first body task, not at workflow launch, and survives checkpoint resume. Task timeouts remain separate. Other tasks may branch.

### Template references

- `prompt.<id>` (`{{prompt.<id>}}`): inject stored prompt text
- `runtime.<key>` (`{{runtime.<key>}}`): value from `runtime_inputs`
- `userinput.<task_id>.value` (`{{userinput.<task_id>.value}}`): earlier `user_input` task
- `task.<task_id>.output...` (`{{task.<task_id>.output...}}`): captured output from an earlier task

### Command selection

Generic workflows should not hardcode `cursor-agent` on every agent task. An **unbound** `command` task omits `function.input.command_id` and inherits a command at launch. A **fixed** task sets a non-empty `command_id` and always runs that command.

For unbound tasks, resolution order is: launch `command_id` (execute request, optional schedule `command_id`, or optional cycle stage `command_id`), then workflow `default_command_id`, then project `default_command_id` in hub `config.json`. Explicit task `command_id` values are not overridden by launch selection.

Unbound task:

```json
{
  "id": "agent_step",
  "name": "Agent work",
  "function": {
    "name": "command",
    "input": { "prompt": "{{prompt.system-implement-story}}" }
  },
  "next_tasks": []
}
```

Fixed task:

```json
{
  "id": "audit_agent",
  "name": "Audit with dedicated command",
  "function": {
    "name": "command",
    "input": {
      "command_id": "audit-system-agent",
      "prompt": "{{prompt.system-audit}}"
    }
  },
  "next_tasks": []
}
```

## Repository guidance workflow

The packaged `system-update-repository-agents` workflow accepts an absolute
`repository_root`, inspects the repository without editing it, and pauses for
answers to questions based on that inspection. After the answer, it rechecks
the source files and updates only the root `AGENTS.md`. It declares a
`command_id` runtime input so launch or project defaults select the inspecting
agent.

## Reference example

From `packages/system-implement-story/1.0.0/definition.json`
(inner `content` pretty-printed; agent task is unbound):

```json
{
  "id": "system-implement-story",
  "name": "Implement story",
  "description": "Runs an installed agent command to implement a single story.",
  "content": {
    "id": "implement-story",
    "name": "Implement story",
    "runtime_inputs": [
      {
        "input_type": "string",
        "key": "story_id",
        "label": "Story id",
        "required": true
      }
    ],
    "tasks": [
      {
        "id": "implement_story",
        "name": "Implement story",
        "function": {
          "name": "command",
          "input": {
            "config": { "cursor_model": "composer-2.5[fast=false]" },
            "prompt": "{{prompt.system-implement-story}}"
          }
        },
        "next_tasks": [
          {
            "id": "report_done",
            "name": "Report completion",
            "function": {
              "name": "cli_command",
              "input": {
                "command": "echo",
                "args": [
                  "implement-story finished for {{runtime.story_id}}"
                ]
              }
            },
            "next_tasks": []
          }
        ]
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

On disk `content` is a nested JSON object, not a string.

## Install path

```json
{
  "to": ".s_e_e/workflows/definitions/system-implement-story.json",
  "from": "packages/implement-story/1.0.0/system-implement-story/definition.json"
}
```

## Schema reference

- Catalog manifest: [`see.library/v1`](/catalog.json)
- Payload contract: [Workflow schema](/schema/workflow/)

# Prompts

Source: /authoring/prompts/

## Prompt homes and references

Choose This machine or Project: Example before creating a prompt. Project files remain under the project's `.s_e_e/prompts/`; machine files are under `~/.s_e_e/definitions/prompts/`. Duplicate ids do not shadow one another. Use `{{prompt.machine:review}}` and `{{prompt.project:review}}` explicitly; bare ids remain project-only. Machine-owned prompts may reference only machine prompts. Missing saved references remain visible for repair.

The picker inserts the canonical reference and opens the chosen home's editor/history. Copy preview shows dependency renames and rewrites. Saving a shared machine prompt affects future uses across projects; delete requires a current usage check. Already captured run content survives source edits/deletion.

MCP named tools and item actions accept qualified ids; omitted scope with a bare id stays project-only, qualified ids infer their home, and disagreeing explicit scope is rejected. Writes require the current conflict token. Project prompt create/update/history/revert use `/api/projects/{code}/definitions/prompts`; machine definitions use `/api/machine/definitions/prompts`. Machine read/edit grants are separate from project access, default off, and edit implies read. Machine MCP advertisements use `machine.<assignment>` and get/completion require an explicit authorized project. Legacy project slug collisions remain explicit rather than ambiguous.

## Prompts that edit Knowledge Drafts

The shared MCP contract prompt describes `knowledge_draft_put`. Pass the current `conflict_token` and include `raw_text` to replace the body. Omit `raw_text` for metadata-only updates. Read back the saved draft before using it as input for further work.

A **prompt** package stores reusable system prompt text referenced by workflows
and commands via the `prompt.<id>` template form
(`{{prompt.<id>}}`). Payload file: `prompt.json`. Installs to
`.s_e_e/prompts/{id}.json`.

## Fields

| Field | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `id` | Stable prompt id (e.g. `system-implement-story`) |
| `name` | Display name in the hub |
| `content` | Prompt body; may include `runtime.*` placeholders (`{{runtime.*}}`) expanded at run time |

## Hub MCP assignment (not in packages)

Installed `prompt.json` files carry only `id`, `name`, and `content`. In the hub
Prompts editor you may assign an MCP prompt name and choose Legacy authoring
arguments, Project only, or up to 32 custom MCP argument rows. Those hub fields
are not part of portable library packages.

## Reference example

From `packages/system-implement-story/1.0.0/prompt.json`:

```json
{
  "id": "system-implement-story",
  "name": "Implement story",
  "content": "You are implementing story {{runtime.story_id}}. Operate fully autonomously..."
}
```

Use a `system-*` id for bundled defaults. Keep template placeholders aligned
with the workflow `runtime_inputs` that declare each `runtime.<key>` placeholder
(`{{runtime.<key>}}`).

## Install path

```json
{
  "to": ".s_e_e/prompts/system-implement-story.json",
  "from": "packages/system-implement-story/1.0.0/prompt.json"
}
```

## Schema reference

- Catalog manifest: [`see.library/v1`](/catalog.json)
- Payload contract: [Prompt schema](/schema/prompt/)

---

# Skills

Source: /authoring/skills/

A **skill** package teaches an agent a repeatable capability. Payload file:
`SKILL.md`. Installs to `.agents/skills/{slug}/SKILL.md`.

## Shape

YAML frontmatter plus markdown body:

- `name`: short skill id (matches the install folder name)
- `description`: activation text; when the user says these phrases, the agent
  should load this skill

The body carries task-specific procedure and constraints that change what the
agent does. Keep activation text short and use authoritative references for
details needed only in particular situations.

## Editing installed skills

GET `/api/projects/:project/spokes/:spoke/agent-skills/:id` returns a
`content` string. PUT accepts `content` and optional `expected_content`, the exact
previously loaded text. Conditional updates require nonempty content and an
existing matching file. Stale or deleted files return 409 without writing;
success remains 204. Omission retains unconditional create or overwrite behavior.
Only `SKILL.md` changes; other skill files are preserved.

```json
{"content":"Updated skill body","expected_content":"Previously loaded skill body"}
```

## Where guidance belongs

Repository `AGENTS.md` holds durable local operating rules. A skill holds
reusable procedure for one capability. A workflow selects the tasks and inputs
for a run; its prompt supplies instructions needed for that task. A story names
one implementation outcome and its acceptance criteria. Agents read the
applicable repository rules and load only the skills and references relevant
to the work. Copying every layer into the first prompt makes repeated and
conflicting guidance harder to maintain.

The current `doc`, `stories`, `workflow`, and `work` skills use the project
store interfaces for installed records. They do not direct agents to edit store
Markdown or workflow JSON on disk. Library package source files remain
editable in this repository before publication. Publish a changed skill as a
new version and refresh any bundle that embeds its payload. Existing
installations need an upgrade to receive that version.

## Write skills for any project

S.E.E. installs `SKILL.md` exactly as written. Do not use `<hub>` or
`<spoke:NAME>` path tokens, and do not copy another project's paths, ids,
languages, or commands into a skill; catalog validation rejects path tokens.
Point agents at the repository `AGENTS.md` for local rules and commands.
Project setup writes a managed S.E.E. section into each project folder's
`AGENTS.md` that names the project id, the `see` MCP server, and where the
S.E.E. skills are installed.

## Reference example

From `packages/work/1.0.1/SKILL.md`:

```markdown
---
name: work
description: >-
  Implement an existing S.E.E. story against its plan and acceptance criteria.
  Use when asked to work on a story id or complete assigned story work.
---

# Work

Read the story through the project store and verify each acceptance criterion.
```

Write the `description` as a single activation sentence agents can match against
user intent. Keep procedures in the markdown body, not in frontmatter.

## Install path

```json
{
  "to": ".agents/skills/work/SKILL.md",
  "from": "packages/work/1.0.1/SKILL.md"
}
```

## Story authoring packages

The bundled `stories` skill and `system-story-authoring` prompt carry the story
specificity review. Broad stories hide affected surfaces and can make partial
work look complete. Apply the specificity review whenever a
story is created or materially revised, before it is handed off, scheduled, or
moved into active work.

Verify the current gap and count affected screens, stored objects, application
code paths, APIs, runtime components, Library definitions, and existing
installations. Name each affected path and exact behavior in the implementation
plan. Split independently deliverable work into separate stories. Give each
affected surface an observable acceptance criterion with evidence beyond the
authored change. Complete and read back any store-created shell in the same
authoring session.

When publishing either authoring package, keep this rule in its payload so
installed agents receive the same guidance. S.E.E. Help, under **Writing
implementation ready stories**, explains the review for people writing or
reviewing stories.

## Milestone authoring packages

The `stories` skill and `system-milestone-authoring` prompt carry the milestone
cut and completion review. Apply it when creating or revising a milestone and
before declaring it Done. A milestone cut names one observable
outcome, includes the stories necessary to deliver it, and states why other
work is deferred.

Assign stories through their milestone field and read membership back. Add a
`milestone_progress` criterion targeting the milestone at 100 percent, then add
separate criteria for the combined outcome and compatibility behavior. Story
acceptance criteria verify individual changes; milestone criteria prove the
release outcome. Check manual criteria only after reviewing their named
evidence. If scope changes, revise the cut, membership, and criteria before
claiming completion.

The Done transition requires at least one member story, self progress at 100
percent, a separate outcome criterion, and every criterion met. Detailed
`milestone_get` shows each criterion's evaluation. Use criteria whose evidence
the milestone store can observe.

Keep this guidance in the published skill and prompt payloads. S.E.E. Help,
under **Authoring milestones and making the cut**, explains the membership and
completion review.

## Schema reference

- Catalog manifest: [`see.library/v1`](/catalog.json)
- Payload contract: [Skill schema](/schema/skill/)

---

# Commands

Source: /authoring/commands/

## Command homes and bindings

Choose This machine or Project: Example before creating a command. Project files remain under the project's `.s_e_e/commands/`; machine files are under `~/.s_e_e/definitions/commands/`. Use `machine:runner` or `project:runner` in workflow defaults, tasks, schedules and cycle stages. Bare ids remain project-only. Same-id commands remain separate; missing or CLI-incompatible choices stay flagged without substitution.

Machine commands can use only machine prompt dependencies. Copy preview identifies dependency rewrites and destination paths before applying. Machine edits affect future uses across projects; current usage and stale previews can block deletion. Authentication settings and server secrets remain application settings rather than definition metadata.

Project command create/update/history/revert use `/api/projects/{code}/definitions/commands`; machine definitions use `/api/machine/definitions/commands`. Reads and writes preserve the selected home; writes require its current conflict token. MCP qualified ids infer scope, while an explicit disagreeing scope is rejected. Machine read/edit grants are independent of project access.

A **command** package defines how the S.E.E. engine runs an external agent CLI
against a spoke workspace. Payload file: `command.json`. Installs to
`.s_e_e/commands/{id}.json`.

## Fields

| Field | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `binary` | Executable name on `PATH` (e.g. `cursor`, `claude`) |
| `base_args` | Arguments always passed before operator overrides |
| `forced_args` | Arguments the engine appends; not overridable |
| `params` | Typed run-time knobs (`string`, `number`, `boolean`, `enum`, `string_array`) mapped to env, timeout, extra args, lock policy, or stream toggle |
| `result` | Success rule (`success_when`), captured fields, optional `applied_paths` and `run_id` strategies |
| `execution` | Working directory (`cwd`: `spoke` or `hub`), lock scope, stream format, `non_interactive` |

Additional fields: `id`, `name`, `icon`, `workspace_arg`, `prompt` delivery,
`env`, and optional `mcp` provisioning.

## Reference example

From `packages/cursor-agent/1.0.0/command.json`:

```json
{
  "id": "cursor-agent",
  "name": "Cursor Agent",
  "binary": "cursor",
  "base_args": ["agent", "-p", "--trust", "--force"],
  "forced_args": ["--output-format", "stream-json", "--stream-partial-output"],
  "params": [
    {
      "key": "cursor_model",
      "type": "string",
      "default": "composer-2.5[fast=false]",
      "map": { "target": "env", "name": "CURSOR_MODEL" }
    },
    {
      "key": "timeout_secs",
      "type": "number",
      "default": 1800,
      "map": { "target": "timeout" }
    }
  ],
  "result": {
    "success_when": "exit_code == 0",
    "capture": ["run_id", "exit_code", "duration_ms", "stdout_tail", "stderr_tail", "truncated"]
  },
  "execution": {
    "cwd": "spoke",
    "lock": { "scope": "spoke", "default_policy": "force" },
    "stream": { "format": "stream-json" },
    "non_interactive": true
  }
}
```

## Install path

Catalog `files[]` entry:

```json
{
  "to": ".s_e_e/commands/cursor-agent.json",
  "from": "packages/cursor-agent/1.0.0/command.json"
}
```

The `to` path must equal `.s_e_e/commands/{id}.json` where `id`
matches `command.json` `id`.

## Codex JSON output

The `success_when` rule supports one comparison of `exit_code` with a signed
32-bit integer using `==`, `!=`, `<`, `<=`, `>` or `>=`, with optional whitespace.
Unsupported expressions fail before the child starts. Generic commands may
accept a configured nonzero code; Codex JSON commands always also require
actual exit code zero.

Codex capture is enabled only when the resolved command has `cliId: "codex"`
and its effective argv contains `--json`. The
`execution.stream.format` field remains unused metadata and does not select a
parser. At actual child exit, output may include `session_id` from
`thread.started.thread_id`, `final_message` from the last completed
`agent_message`, `usage` from `turn.completed.usage`, and `codex_terminal`
containing the latest `turn.completed` or `turn.failed` event. Capture and
terminal failures add `codex_error`. These fields preserve SEE's `run_id`,
actual process `exit_code`, duration, and output tails.

Codex task success requires the actual child exit code to be zero, the
configured `success_when` rule to pass, and the latest turn to end with
`turn.completed`. A failed or missing terminal turn, nonzero exit, or frame or
final-message size over 4,194,304 bytes fails the task. A later `turn.started`
makes the previous terminal event incomplete. Recovered standalone errors do
not fail a completed turn. Capture retains only current thread id, last
completed assistant message, latest terminal event, usage, and failure detail.
Automatic agent JSON merging uses only a complete `final_message` that parses
as a JSON object. Explicit `result.extract[]` behavior continues to use its
configured stdout/stderr source and path.

Codex transport failures keep the existing four-attempt retry bound when the
child exits nonzero, stderr contains `RetriableError`, and no terminal event or
capture-size failure was received. Each attempt starts with fresh capture
metadata. Failed terminal turns, zero-exit incomplete streams, capture-size
failures and success-rule mismatches are not retried. Cancellation and timeout
keep their existing cleanup behavior. Command success does not verify story
criteria or mark a story Done.

## Schema reference

- Catalog manifest: [`see.library/v1`](/catalog.json)
- Payload contract: [Command schema](/schema/command/)

---

# Bundles

Source: /authoring/bundles/

## Library destinations

This machine is available only when the complete package/dependency/member closure contains prompts, commands, workflows or definition-only bundles. A mixed bundle containing a skill, starter, cycle, schedule, rule set or knowledge document is project-only. Preview the concrete destination before installing. Project: Example keeps existing `.s_e_e/` package paths; This machine maps definition files into `~/.s_e_e/definitions/` and keeps independent installed state there. Package metadata and old project installations remain compatible; startup does not migrate or seed machine definitions.

Package workflow `spoke_root` values are removed with a visible preview when copying into the machine home. Direct machine workflow saves must omit `spoke_root`. Dependencies are rewritten to machine references; explicitly review reuse or renamed definitions. Copy/install leaves the source and existing bindings intact.

The same package can be installed independently in both homes. Update/uninstall retains the reviewed home even after project switching. Local edits require acknowledgement; usage, inaccessible projects and stale previews can block removal. Project backups do not contain machine definitions: back up `~/.s_e_e/definitions/` separately. Runs, logs, schedules, cycles and execution history remain project-owned.

A **bundle** installs several library packages together. It has no payload file
of its own; the catalog entry `files[]` lists every member install map.

## Metadata (`s_e_e_package.json`)

Each bundle carries a sidecar at `packages/{slug}/s_e_e_package.json`:

```json
{
  "id": "bundle-implement-story",
  "slug": "implement-story",
  "category": "bundle",
  "name": "Implement Story workflows",
  "description": "Packages linked by template references: workflows, prompts, skills, commands.",
  "labels": ["bulk", "story"],
  "dependencies": [],
  "toolIds": ["cursor"],
  "releases": [
    { "version": "1.0.0", "date": "2026-09-01", "note": "Initial catalog release." }
  ]
}
```

| Field | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `id` | Globally unique package id (`bundle-<slug>`) |
| `slug` | URL-safe folder name under `packages/` |
| `category` | Must be `bundle` |
| `name`, `description` | Catalog presentation |
| `labels` | Discovery tags |
| `dependencies` | Other package ids installed alongside this bundle |
| `toolIds` | Declared tool ids, or `[]` when uncategorized |
| `releases` | `{ version, date, note }` history |

## Members

When harvesting from a local hub, `scripts/bundles.json` lists member package
ids per bundle slug. The harvest script copies each member payload into
`packages/{bundle-slug}/{version}/` and builds the catalog `files[]` array.
Hand-authored bundles list every `to`/`from` pair directly in `catalog.json`.

Marketplace stacks are a different source. `scripts/stacks.json` declares
`sharedPackageIds`, per-tool `variants`, and `featuredStackId`. A bundle is an
install map; a stack is a source-owned grouping that can install one tool path.

Example members for `implement-story` (from `scripts/bundles.json`):

- `cmd-cursor-agent`
- `prompt-system-implement-story`
- `skill-work`
- `wf-system-implement-story`
- `wf-system-implement-stories-bulk`

The `knowledge-system` bundle is hand-authored in `catalog.json` and installs
the seven knowledge loop definitions, their prompts, the commands they spawn,
and disabled schedules.

## Install map

Each entry maps a repo path to an install target:

```json
{
  "to": ".s_e_e/prompts/system-implement-story.json",
  "from": "packages/implement-story/1.0.0/system-implement-story/prompt.json"
}
```

The build infers payload kind from the `to` prefix:

- `.s_e_e/workflows/definitions/` is a workflow;
- `.s_e_e/workflows/schedules/` is a schedule;
- `.s_e_e/workflows/schedule_rule_sets/` is a schedule rule set;
- `.s_e_e/prompts/` is a prompt;
- `.s_e_e/commands/` is a command;
- `.s_e_e/knowledge/` is a knowledge markdown payload (for example the component inventory template);
- `.agents/skills/` is a skill;
- `.cursor/` is a rule;
- `templates/` is a template.
- `.s_e_e/cycles/` is a cycle document.

## Install path rules

Every `files[]` `to` path must start with one of:

- `.s_e_e/`
- `.agents/`
- `.cursor/`
- `templates/`

Paths use forward slashes and must be unique within the package.

## Schema reference

- Catalog manifest: [`see.library/v2`](/catalog.json)
- Payload contract: [Bundle schema](/schema/bundle/)
- [Schedule schema](/schema/schedule/)
- [Schedule rule set schema](/schema/schedule-rule-set/)

---

# Cycles

Source: /authoring/cycles/

Project settings > Experimental controls host availability. Orchestrator requires `orchestrator` and `orchestrator_cycle`, Knowledge requires `knowledge_cycle`, and Planning requires `planning_cycle`. All default to false. Disabled hosts are omitted from cycle management and their launch, edit, activation and revert operations are denied. Stored cycle packages, reusable workflow definitions and Library package storage remain available.

Disabling preserves schedules and saved run controls and does not cancel admitted work. It suppresses fresh timer, catchup, event and manual admission. Generic execution, process, log and stop controls remain available. Subsequent disabled feature-owned operations fail explicitly with `EXPERIMENTAL_FEATURE_DISABLED`. Enabling may resume scheduled work on the next normal tick. Manual story and milestone planning remains available. There is no Planning cycle-control HTTP endpoint or manual-stage HTTP route.

A **cycle** package describes how workflows connect stores on a host. Payload
file: `cycle.json`. Installs to `.s_e_e/cycles/{id}.json` where `id` matches the
document `id` field.

## Stages and stores

Each **stage** runs one workflow definition. It `reads` zero or more store keys
and `writes` exactly one store key. The `stores` array lists every key the cycle
touches.

**One writer per store:** at most one stage may write a given store key on the
orchestrator host.

## Triggers

Each stage has exactly one trigger: `tick`, `schedule`, `event`, or `manual`.

## Saving edits

Existing cycle edits use the revision returned when the document was loaded. A stale revision, including one for a deleted document, is rejected without overwriting newer data. Reload revision retains local edits; use Save to apply them after reviewing the changes. Saving does not activate a different cycle or request a run.

## Store registry

Store keys are not free-form. The app ships a fixed registry per host. A key
outside the list is rejected on install and reported again at activation.

**Orchestrator host:** `world`, `objectives`, `deliberations`, `ranking`,
`proposals`, `executions`, `learning`.

**Knowledge host:** `spokes`, `changes`, `components`, `impacts`, `audits`,
`docs`, `decisions`, `links`.

The JSON Schema allows `stories` and `events` as host values. Planning uses the stories host when planning_cycle is enabled. Events has no Experimental switch.

## The orchestrator gate

On the orchestrator host, the `propose` stage is the **gate**. It is compiled
into the app: you cannot declare a different gate stage, remove it, or change
its reads, writes, workflow, or trigger.

## Activation checks

Errors block activation: `unknown_store`, `store_has_two_writers`,
`stage_has_no_reads`, `workflow_not_installed`, `gate_missing`, `gate_rewired`.
Warnings do not block activation.

## Reference example

From `packages/cycle-orchestrator-default/1.0.0/cycle.json` (five orchestrator
stages, all `tick`; the `propose` stage uses the compiled `create_proposal`
gate). The package depends on the four catalog workflow packages those stages
need. The compiled gate has no catalog package.

From `packages/cycle-knowledge-default/1.0.0/cycle.json` (seven knowledge
stages, mixed triggers).

The full files in the catalog list every stage.

## Install path

```json
{
  "to": ".s_e_e/cycles/cycle-orchestrator-default.json",
  "from": "packages/cycle-orchestrator-default/1.0.0/cycle.json"
}
```

```json
{
  "to": ".s_e_e/cycles/cycle-knowledge-default.json",
  "from": "packages/cycle-knowledge-default/1.0.0/cycle.json"
}
```

## Schema reference

- Catalog manifest: [`see.library/v1`](/catalog.json)
- Payload contract: [Cycle schema](/schema/cycle/)

---

# Publish to the catalog

Source: /authoring/publish/

After authoring a package payload, add it to this repository and validate before
opening a pull request.

## Payload layout

Place files under:

```
packages/{slug}/{version}/
```

Examples:

- `packages/cursor-agent/1.0.0/command.json`
- `packages/system-implement-story/1.0.0/prompt.json`
- `packages/work/1.0.0/SKILL.md`
- `packages/implement-story/1.0.0/system-implement-story/definition.json`

Add `packages/{slug}/s_e_e_package.json` metadata for every catalog entry.

Bundles copy member payloads under the bundle slug folder, for example
`packages/implement-story/1.0.0/work/SKILL.md`.

## `catalog.json` entry

Append a package object to `catalog.json` `packages[]`:

| Field | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `id` | Globally unique id (e.g. `cmd-cursor-agent`, `bundle-implement-story`) |
| `slug` | URL-safe slug matching the `packages/` folder |
| `category` | `workflow`, `prompt`, `skill`, `command`, or `bundle` |
| `version` | Semver string (e.g. `1.0.0`) |
| `author` | Publisher id |
| `verified` | `true` when signed off by a maintainer |
| `license` | SPDX id (e.g. `AGPL-3.0-only`) |
| `requires` | External tools required at install time (empty array when none) |
| `dependencies` | Other package `id`s installed alongside this one |
| `files[]` | Install map with `to` and `from` paths |

Optional presentation fields: `name`, `description`, `labels`.

Marketplace and classification fields live on the sidecar and are copied into
the catalog. Do not hand-edit them on `catalog.json`.

## Classification (required for new packages)

| Field | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `usageContexts` | Non-empty array of `cycle` or `standalone` |
| `cliScope` | `{ scope: "any" }` or `{ scope: "specific", cliIds: [...] }` referencing `tools[]` |
| `toolIds` | CLI tool ids; use `[]` with `cliScope.scope: any` |
| `releases` | `{ version, date, note }` history for the package |

Older entries without classification still install; the hub infers scopes from `category` and legacy `toolIds` until republished.

Stacks, the tool registry, and featured selection live in `scripts/stacks.json`:

```json
{
  "tools": [
    { "id": "cursor", "name": "Cursor" },
    { "id": "claude", "name": "Claude Code" }
  ],
  "featuredStackId": "stack-implement-story",
  "stacks": [
    {
      "id": "stack-implement-story",
      "name": "Implement story",
      "sharedPackageIds": ["wf-system-implement-story", "skill-work"],
      "variants": [
        { "toolId": "cursor", "packageIds": ["cmd-cursor-agent"] },
        { "toolId": "claude", "packageIds": ["cmd-claude-code"] }
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

Example command entry:

```json
{
  "id": "cmd-cursor-agent",
  "slug": "cursor-agent",
  "category": "command",
  "version": "1.0.0",
  "author": "garunski",
  "verified": true,
  "license": "AGPL-3.0-only",
  "requires": [],
  "dependencies": [],
  "files": [
    {
      "to": ".s_e_e/commands/cursor-agent.json",
      "from": "packages/cursor-agent/1.0.0/command.json"
    }
  ],
  "name": "Cursor Agent",
  "description": "Cursor CLI agent run against a spoke workspace."
}
```

## Validate and build

```bash
mise run validate
mise run catalog
```

- `mise run validate` runs `see_library_catalog_tool validate` (read-only;
  fails when payloads or metadata are invalid or out of sync).
- `mise run catalog` validates payloads, refreshes `catalog.json` `updated`, and
  writes any derived fields.
- `mise run harvest` copies hub payloads into `packages/` and regenerates
  `catalog.json` when publishing from a local hub checkout.

After merge, installers resolve the package by catalog `id` and `version`. The
`files[]` install map is authoritative: each `from` path under `packages/` maps
to a hub `to` destination. Keep `id`, `version`, and `files[]` stable across
releases unless you intend a breaking catalog change.

Commit both the payload under `packages/` and the updated `catalog.json`.

## Docs site

`mise run site-build` exports the Dioxus static site and
copies root `catalog.json` and `packages/` into the publish output so GitHub
Pages serves them at the same public URLs.

A new package type also needs a section in `public/llms.txt`, which carries the
same guidance as one plain-text file for agents. Keep the page and
`Source: /authoring/publish/` section in sync.

## Schema reference

- Catalog manifest: [`see.library/v2`](/catalog.json)
- Payload contract: [Catalog schema](/schema/catalog/)

## Knowledge

Component updates at `/api/projects/{project}/knowledge/components/{id}` require the current conflict token. PUT accepts `body`, `verified_against`, and `conflict_token`. A stale token or superseded note returns `409 WORKSPACE_CONFLICT` with the current note and token without creating a revision. Success creates a new current note: use its returned id and token for subsequent updates.

- [Knowledge Research](/schema/knowledge-research/)
