# Catalog schema

Source: /schema/catalog/

The catalog is a single JSON manifest (`catalog.json`) plus versioned payload
files under `packages/`. The manifest schema tag is `see.library/v1` or
`see.library/v2`. This section is the authoritative contract for this
repository; `scripts/build-catalog.mjs` enforces it.

## Manifest

`catalog.json`:

- `schema` - `see.library/v1` or `see.library/v2`.
- `name` - catalog display name.
- `updated` - ISO-8601 timestamp (refreshed by `npm run build`).
- `packages[]` - array of package entries.
- `tools[]` - optional CLI tool registry (`id`, `name`, optional `description`). v1 catalogs omit this and parse as empty.
- `stacks[]` - optional source-owned stacks with `sharedPackageIds` and `variants`.
- `featuredStackId` - optional id of one declared stack.

## Package entry

Each entry in `packages[]`:

- `id` - string, globally unique within the catalog.
- `slug` - string, url/file-safe.
- `category` - one of `workflow`, `prompt`, `skill`, `rule`, `template`, `command`, `bundle`, `cycle`.
- `version` - semver string.
- `author` - string.
- `verified` - bool.
- `license` - SPDX id (e.g. `AGPL-3.0-only`).
- `requires` - string array of external tools that must be present (empty when none).
- `dependencies` - string array of other package `id`s installed alongside this one.
- `files[]` - install map; each entry is `{ to, from }`:
  - `from` - source path in this repo, `packages/{slug}/{version}/{file}`.
  - `to` - destination path written on the install target, relative to the target root.
- `toolIds` - optional declared CLI tool ids (legacy). Prefer `cliScope` for new packages.
- `usageContexts` - optional `cycle` or `standalone` (required on new packages).
- `cliScope` - `{ scope: "any" }` or `{ scope: "specific", cliIds: [...] }` referencing `tools[]`.
- `releases` - optional `{ version, date, note }` history for the package.

## Legacy classification inference

Packages published before explicit classification omit `usageContexts`, `cliScope`. They still parse and install. The hub infers:

- `usageContexts`: `cycle` when `category` is `cycle`, otherwise `standalone`.
- `cliScope`: `any` when `toolIds` is empty; `specific` with those ids when non-empty.

API responses mark each dimension as authored or inferred without rewriting catalog source files.

## Stacks

A stack is source-owned, not a local collection. Author stacks in
`scripts/stacks.json`. `sharedPackageIds` lists packages every variant
installs. Each variant names a declared `toolId` and additional `packageIds`.
`featuredStackId` must be one declared stack id.

```json
{
  "tools": [
    { "id": "cursor", "name": "Cursor" },
    { "id": "claude", "name": "Claude Code" }
  ],
  "featuredStackId": "stack-implement-story",
  "stacks": [
    {
      "id": "stack-implement-story",
      "name": "Implement story",
      "description": "Shared implement-story packages plus one agent CLI.",
      "sharedPackageIds": [
        "wf-system-implement-story",
        "prompt-system-implement-story",
        "skill-work"
      ],
      "variants": [
        { "toolId": "cursor", "packageIds": ["cmd-cursor-agent"] },
        { "toolId": "claude", "packageIds": ["cmd-claude-code"] }
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

## Package metadata sidecar

Every package carries a `packages/{slug}/s_e_e_package.json` (or
`s_e_e_package.{id}.json` when a slug has multiple entries); the build
cross-checks it against the catalog entry:

- `id` - package id; matches the catalog entry.
- `slug` - url/file-safe slug.
- `category` - one of the category values above.
- `name` - display name.
- `description` - one-line summary.
- `labels` - string array (the build dedupes and sorts it).
- `dependencies` - string array of other package `id`s.
- `toolIds` - declared tool registry ids. Required. Use `[]` when the package is deliberately uncategorized. The build copies this array; it never infers a tool from name or path.
- `releases` - required `{ version, date, note }` history. The catalog emits these rows; do not hand-edit them on `catalog.json`.

## Categories

Each category has a fixed payload shape and install destination:

- `workflow` - a workflow definition JSON. Installs to `.s_e_e/workflows/definitions/{slug}.json`.
- `prompt` - a prompt JSON (`id`, `name`, `content`). Installs to `.s_e_e/prompts/{file}.json`.
- `skill` - a `SKILL.md` with `name` + `description` frontmatter. Installs to `.agents/skills/{slug}/SKILL.md`.
- `rule` - a Cursor rule `.mdc` file. Installs to `.cursor/rules/{slug}.mdc`.
- `template` - a scaffold file. Installs under `templates/`.
- `command` - a command definition JSON (`id`, `binary`). Installs to `.s_e_e/commands/{id}.json` (the `to` path must equal this exactly).
- `bundle` - no payload of its own; its `files[]` install several other packages together. The build infers each file's kind from its `to` path.
- `cycle` - a cycle document JSON. Installs to `.s_e_e/cycles/{id}.json` (the `to` path must match the document `id`).

## Install paths

Every `files[]` `to` path must:

- start with one of `.s_e_e/`, `.agents/`, `.cursor/`, or `templates/`;
- use forward slashes;
- be unique within the package.

For a `bundle`, the `to` prefix determines the payload kind that is validated:

- `.s_e_e/workflows/definitions/…` validates as a workflow;
- `.s_e_e/prompts/…` validates as a prompt;
- `.s_e_e/commands/…` validates as a command;
- `.s_e_e/knowledge/…` validates as a knowledge markdown payload;
- `.s_e_e/workflows/schedules/…` validates as a schedule;
- `.s_e_e/workflows/schedule_rule_sets/…` validates as a schedule rule set;
- `.agents/skills/…/SKILL.md` validates as a skill;
- `*.mdc` validates as a rule;
- `templates/…` validates as a template.
- `.s_e_e/cycles/…` validates as a cycle document.

## Validation

`dependencies` must reference package `id`s present in the catalog, and a
package cannot depend on itself. v2 marketplace metadata rejects duplicate tool
or stack ids, unknown package `toolIds`, unknown stack package ids, and variants
that name an undeclared tool. Run `npm run build` to validate payloads and
refresh the manifest, or `npm run validate` (`--check`, no writes) in CI.

## JSON Schema

Download: [catalog.schema.json](https://garunski.github.io/s_e_e_library/schema/catalog.schema.json)

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "$id": "https://garunski.github.io/s_e_e_library/schema/catalog.schema.json",
  "title": "S.E.E. Library catalog manifest",
  "type": "object",
  "required": [
    "schema",
    "name",
    "packages"
  ],
  "properties": {
    "schema": {
      "enum": [
        "see.library/v1",
        "see.library/v2"
      ]
    },
    "name": {
      "type": "string",
      "minLength": 1
    },
    "updated": {
      "type": "string",
      "format": "date-time"
    },
    "packages": {
      "type": "array",
      "items": {
        "$ref": "#/$defs/package"
      }
    },
    "tools": {
      "type": "array",
      "items": {
        "$ref": "#/$defs/tool"
      }
    },
    "stacks": {
      "type": "array",
      "items": {
        "$ref": "#/$defs/stack"
      }
    },
    "featuredStackId": {
      "type": "string",
      "minLength": 1
    }
  },
  "$defs": {
    "package": {
      "type": "object",
      "required": [
        "id",
        "slug",
        "category",
        "version",
        "author",
        "verified",
        "license",
        "requires",
        "dependencies",
        "files"
      ],
      "properties": {
        "id": {
          "type": "string",
          "minLength": 1
        },
        "slug": {
          "type": "string",
          "minLength": 1
        },
        "category": {
          "enum": [
            "workflow",
            "prompt",
            "skill",
            "rule",
            "template",
            "command",
            "bundle",
            "cycle"
          ]
        },
        "version": {
          "type": "string",
          "minLength": 1
        },
        "author": {
          "type": "string"
        },
        "verified": {
          "type": "boolean"
        },
        "license": {
          "type": "string"
        },
        "requires": {
          "type": "array",
          "items": {
            "type": "string"
          }
        },
        "dependencies": {
          "type": "array",
          "items": {
            "type": "string",
            "minLength": 1
          }
        },
        "name": {
          "type": "string"
        },
        "description": {
          "type": "string"
        },
        "labels": {
          "type": "array",
          "items": {
            "type": "string",
            "minLength": 1
          }
        },
        "toolIds": {
          "type": "array",
          "items": {
            "type": "string",
            "minLength": 1
          }
        },
        "usageContexts": {
          "type": "array",
          "items": {
            "type": "string",
            "enum": [
              "cycle",
              "standalone"
            ]
          }
        },
        "cliScope": {
          "$ref": "#/$defs/cliScope"
        },
        "releases": {
          "type": "array",
          "items": {
            "$ref": "#/$defs/release"
          }
        },
        "files": {
          "type": "array",
          "minItems": 1,
          "items": {
            "$ref": "#/$defs/file"
          }
        }
      }
    },
    "file": {
      "type": "object",
      "required": [
        "to",
        "from"
      ],
      "properties": {
        "to": {
          "type": "string",
          "pattern": "^(\\.s_e_e/|\\.agents/|\\.cursor/|templates/)[^\\\\]*$"
        },
        "from": {
          "type": "string",
          "minLength": 1
        }
      }
    },
    "tool": {
      "type": "object",
      "required": [
        "id",
        "name"
      ],
      "properties": {
        "id": {
          "type": "string",
          "minLength": 1
        },
        "name": {
          "type": "string",
          "minLength": 1
        },
        "description": {
          "type": "string"
        }
      }
    },
    "cliScope": {
      "oneOf": [
        {
          "type": "object",
          "required": [
            "scope"
          ],
          "properties": {
            "scope": {
              "const": "any"
            }
          },
          "additionalProperties": true
        },
        {
          "type": "object",
          "required": [
            "scope",
            "cliIds"
          ],
          "properties": {
            "scope": {
              "const": "specific"
            },

              "type": "array",
              "minItems": 1,
              "items": {

                "minLength": 1
              }
            }
          },
          "additionalProperties": true
        }
      ]
    },
    "release": {
      "type": "object",
      "required": [
        "version",
        "date",
        "note"
      ],
      "properties": {
        "version": {

      }

}
```

# Workflow schema

Source: /schema/workflow/

## Definition homes

The home labels are This machine and Project: Example.

This machine contains definitions for the current OS user.

Machine definitions are stored under ~/.s_e_e/definitions/.

Workflow runs, logs, schedules, cycles, and execution history remain per project.

Machine definitions are outside project Git and project backups; back up ~/.s_e_e/definitions/ separately.

A machine workflow runs only after a target project is selected.

Prompts, commands and workflow definitions can live in either home. Duplicate ids and names remain distinct; neither home shadows the other. `machine:review` selects the machine definition; `project:review` selects the target project's definition. A bare `review` remains project-only. Prompt templates use `{{prompt.machine:review}}` or `{{prompt.project:review}}`; legacy `{{prompt.review}}` stays project-only. Missing or incompatible selections stay flagged for repair and are never replaced by the same id in another home.

Machine workflows must omit `spoke_root` everywhere in their content and cannot depend on project-only prompts or commands. Their working context comes from the selected project at launch. Project workflows may use either home. Schedules, cycle stages and project defaults store explicit references but keep their project owner. A run captures definition content, exact home and revision; later edits or deletion do not rewrite that snapshot. Legacy runs with no captured provenance remain unknown.

Definition search retains exact home, kind, path and editor destination for duplicate names. Machine-only search works without selecting a project and exposes only authorized prompt, command and workflow metadata, never project business data. HTTP uses `/api/machine/definitions/search`; selected-project search stays under `/api/projects/{code}/search`. Denied machine access and unauthorized projects do not expose titles, snippets or counts. Reopening search refreshes definition revisions.

Copy previews identify the source, destination, concrete paths and dependency rewrites. Review renamed dependencies and explicit reuse before applying the preview token. Copying leaves the original and existing bindings intact. Editing a machine definition affects future uses across projects. Deletion checks project usage; stale or inaccessible usage blocks deletion. Existing runs retain captured content.

Client grants separate project access from machine definition read/edit permissions. Machine access defaults off; edit implies read. A project-only worker token cannot edit machine definitions. Machine prompt discovery requires machine read and an explicit authorized target project for expansion; project access alone does not grant machine access.

The workflow guide examples use one machine workflow with two different explicit project targets in `workflow_execute` arguments. They illustrate request structure; execution ownership is verified separately. No machine execution endpoint is introduced.

### Machine workflow and launch arguments

Stored definition (no spoke_root):

```json
{
  "id": "review",
  "name": "Review",
  "version": 1,
  "is_edited": false,
  "created_at": "2026-11-07T00:00:00Z",
  "updated_at": "2026-11-07T00:00:00Z",
  "content": {
    "id": "review",
    "name": "Review",
    "tasks": [{"id": "inspect", "name": "Inspect", "function": {"name": "cli_command", "input": {"command": "git", "args": ["status", "--short"]}}}]
  }
}
```

workflow_execute for project-a:

```json
{"project":"project-a","workflow_id":"machine:review","runtime_inputs":{}}
```

workflow_execute for project-b:

```json
{"project":"project-b","workflow_id":"machine:review","runtime_inputs":{}}
```

See [prompt details](/s_e_e_library/authoring/prompts/), [command details](/s_e_e_library/authoring/commands/) and [Library destinations](/s_e_e_library/authoring/bundles/).

## Collection selection arguments

Existing collection tools accept a shared `filters` member. `list_filter_get` with `project` and `collection` returns supported fields, operators, nullable behavior and enum choices. [collection-filter.schema.json](/schema/collection-filter.schema.json) owns predicate shapes and bounds. Descriptor validation enforces same-type operands, enum choices and collection-specific rules. HTTP GET encodes one JSON array. Project, legacy selectors and paging remain operation-specific. The examples and correction guidance are in the workflow authoring section above.

## Execution runtime and controls

Definitions retain their nested authoring form. Execution uses a flat graph of task IDs and materializes one foreach iteration and one repair attempt at a time. A loop's `wait_for` barrier completes only after the whole loop, including its verifiers, succeeds. An empty successful loop contributes zero action records.

Each run has a supervised worker process. The parent API owns durable execution writes and terminal status. Worker signal exits, nonzero exits, missing terminal exchange and malformed IPC produce a failed run with `worker_aborted` or `worker_protocol_error`. The saved worker failure includes the exit code or signal and a bounded stderr tail. The API and other isolated runs can continue after a worker abort. Host-wide failures can still affect the parent and workers; machine-wide fault isolation is not guaranteed.

**Pause** records a request immediately, stops new admissions and waits for already active steps. The run becomes **Paused** after those steps settle and the checkpoint is saved. Repeated pause requests are idempotent. **Cancel** stops the run and terminates its owned worker and command descendants, with a two-second grace before forced cleanup. Parent disconnect and server shutdown also clean up owned workers and descendants. A control timeout or closed pipe is recorded as cancellation or worker failure, never as a successful pause acknowledgment.

**Resume** continues a safely checkpointed paused run without replaying completed task IDs or losing their outputs. Current checkpoints contain flat graph state, loop cursors, outputs, allocation counters, resource policy and frozen run provenance. Unknown in-flight actions after an interruption are recorded as failures and are not automatically replayed. Reconcile uncertain external side effects before starting replacement work. Exactly-once external effects are not guaranteed. The engine reads the current flat checkpoint format only.

## Progress fields

HTTP execution reads and MCP `execution_get` expose the same `runtime_progress` object. `status` remains authoritative; successful worker startup does not mean Complete.

| Field | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `materialized_tasks`, `completed_tasks` | Actual action IDs currently materialized and completed; templates and loop control barriers are excluded |
| `total_tasks` | `null` while future loop work remains unknown; consumers must omit a percentage instead of showing 100 percent from current materialization |
| `generated_nodes`, `generated_edges` | Lifetime allocations, retained across resume |
| `retained_nodes`, `retained_edges` | Current retained graph size, including templates and controls |
| `loops[].collection_size` | Known foreach collection size, or `null` until its producer resolves |
| `loops[].current_iteration` | Zero-based active foreach index, or `null` |
| `loops[].completed_iterations` | Successfully completed foreach iterations; after item zero of 39 this is 1 of 39 and the barrier is pending |
| `loops[].active_attempt` | One-based active repair attempt, or `null` |
| `loops[].barrier_pending` | Whether the complete loop barrier is still pending |
| `pause_requested` | A request is pending; this differs from a committed Paused state |
| `worker_pid`, `worker_failure` | Owned worker identity and bounded failure diagnostics, when available |

## Resource limits

The policy is selected at launch and preserved on resume. Limits are checked before graph mutation or semantic output retention. A rejected semantic result is not silently truncated into apparently valid task output.

| Limit name | Default |
| --- | --- |
| `authored_bytes` | 8 MiB |
| `authored_depth` | 64 |
| `generated_nodes` | 100,000 over the run's lifetime |
| `generated_edges` | 200,000 over the run's lifetime |
| `foreach_items` | 10,000 per collection |
| `active_handlers` | 32 |
| `task_result_bytes` | 1 MiB encoded structured result |
| `retained_result_bytes` | 64 MiB aggregate retained results |
| `checkpoint_bytes` | 128 MiB encoded checkpoint |

`resource_limit_exceeded` identifies the limit, allowed amount, attempted amount, task ID and execution ID. An HTTP request rejected before acceptance uses the `{error, code?}` envelope. An accepted run reports finite failure details in `errors`; worker failures also use `runtime_progress.worker_failure`. Retained prior outputs and completed evidence remain available after a limit failure.

Worker IPC has a 1 MiB frame body, a 64-frame bounded queue and a 128 MiB total chunked-checkpoint limit. Worker stderr retention uses three 5 MiB files and a 64 KiB diagnostic tail, with dropped-byte accounting. Diagnostic tails may omit bytes; semantic captured JSON must remain complete or fail.

Published response schemas: workflow-execution.schema.json and execution-error.schema.json.


Category `workflow`. Payload file `definition.json`. Installs to
`.s_e_e/workflows/definitions/{slug}.json`.

An outer envelope wraps the engine `content`:

- `id` - `system-<name>` (defaults) or `user-<name>`. Required.
- `name`, `description`, `version` - strings.
- `content` - the engine workflow object:
  - `id` - required, non-empty.
  - `name` - required.
  - `tasks[]` - required, non-empty.
  - `runtime_inputs[]` - optional; each `{ key, input_type, required, label }`; `key` must not contain dots.
  - `default_command_id` - optional installed command id for `command` tasks that omit `function.input.command_id`.
  - `spoke_root`, `hub_root`, `stories_root`, `knowledge_root` - optional root paths. An exact `{{runtime.KEY}}` value resolves from a string run input before execution and resume. The resulting path must exist and be absolute. Hub-scoped runs may inject hub and store roots from the project. When `spoke_root` is omitted, the run uses the project's code folder for story implementation and code knowledge workflows and the project home folder otherwise.

## Tasks

Each task:

- `id` - unique within the workflow.
- `name` - string.
- `function` - exactly one handler key: `cli_command`, `command`, `user_input`, `git_action`, `s_e_e_action`, `foreach`, or `custom`.

`s_e_e_action` calls one MCP tool. `input.tool` is the precise named tool id. `item_call` remains for a call that has no named tool. `input.arguments` is that tool's argument object and includes an explicit `project` such as `{{project.id}}`. Tool names are in the Tools reference.

- `next_tasks[]` - optional nested authoring form compiled to flat dependencies. `foreach` must have exactly one, and that body must be one chain with a single leaf. A later branch is rejected. Nested `foreach` is allowed when each body is still one chain. `repair_loop` is a one-leaf body, then one verifier. Other tasks may branch.
- `capture_output` - when true, record handler output for `{{task.TASK_ID.output}}` placeholders.
- `wait_for` - task ids that must complete before this task runs (use a foreach id to wait for all iterations).
- `continue_on_failure` - when true, a failed task completes without failing the workflow; output is still captured when `capture_output` is true.
- `run_when` - object `{ task, path?, op, value? }` gating this task on the captured output of a prior task (`op`: `eq`, `ne`, `gt`, `lt`, `ge`, `le`, `exists`).

A payload containing `tasks` is treated as a workflow (not a prompt).

## Command tasks

Handler `command` runs an installed definition from `.s_e_e/commands/`. Omit `command_id` for an unbound task; set a non-empty `command_id` to fix the task. Empty `command_id` strings are invalid.

Unbound tasks resolve at launch: launch `command_id` (execute request, schedule `command_id`, or cycle stage `command_id`), then workflow `default_command_id`, then project `default_command_id` in hub `config.json`. Fixed task `command_id` values are not overridden by launch selection.

## Template expansion

```
{{prompt.ID}}              injects a stored prompt; the id must exist in the hub
{{runtime.KEY}}            run-start value; declared in runtime_inputs, no dots
{{userinput.TASK_ID.value}} value from an earlier user_input task
{{task.TASK_ID.output}}    captured output from an earlier task with capture_output: true
                           (cli_command output is { exit_code, stdout, stderr })
```

## JSON Schema

Download: [workflow.schema.json](https://garunski.github.io/s_e_e_library/schema/workflow.schema.json)

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "$id": "https://garunski.github.io/s_e_e_library/schema/workflow.schema.json",
  "title": "Workflow package payload (definition.json)",
  "type": "object",
  "required": ["id", "name", "content"],
  "properties": {
    "id": { "type": "string", "minLength": 1 },
    "name": { "type": "string", "minLength": 1 },
    "description": { "type": "string" },
    "version": { "type": "string" },
    "content": { "$ref": "#/$defs/workflow" }
  },
  "$defs": {
    "workflow": {
      "type": "object",
      "required": ["id", "name", "tasks"],
      "properties": {
        "id": { "type": "string", "minLength": 1 },
        "name": { "type": "string", "minLength": 1 },
        "spoke_root": { "type": "string", "description": "Existing absolute directory or exact {{runtime.KEY}} reference to a string runtime input" },
        "hub_root": { "type": "string" },
        "stories_root": { "type": "string" },
        "knowledge_root": { "type": "string" },
        "runtime_inputs": {
          "type": "array",
          "items": { "$ref": "#/$defs/runtime_input" }
        },
        "default_command_id": {
          "type": "string",
          "minLength": 1,
          "description": "Optional default for command tasks that omit command_id"
        },
        "tasks": {
          "type": "array",
          "minItems": 1,
          "items": { "$ref": "#/$defs/task" }
        }
      }
    },
    "runtime_input": {
      "type": "object",
      "required": ["key", "input_type"],
      "properties": {
        "key": {
          "type": "string",
          "pattern": "^[^.]+$",
          "description": "Referenced as {{runtime.KEY}}; no dots."
        },
        "input_type": { "type": "string" },
        "required": { "type": "boolean" },
        "label": { "type": "string" }
      }
    },
    "task": {
      "type": "object",
      "required": ["id", "name", "function"],
      "properties": {
        "id": { "type": "string", "minLength": 1 },
        "name": { "type": "string" },
        "function": { "$ref": "#/$defs/function" },
        "next_tasks": {
          "type": "array",
          "items": { "$ref": "#/$defs/task" }
        },
        "capture_output": {
          "type": "boolean",
          "default": false,
          "description": "Record handler output for `{{task.<id>.output...}}` templates"
        },
        "wait_for": {
          "type": "array",
          "items": { "type": "string", "minLength": 1 },
          "description": "Task ids that must complete before this task runs"
        },
        "continue_on_failure": {
          "type": "boolean",
          "default": false,
          "description": "Treat a failed task as complete so descendants and captured output stay reachable"
        },
        "run_when": {
          "$ref": "#/$defs/condition",
          "description": "Gate execution on a prior task's captured output"
        }
      }
    },
    "condition": {
      "type": "object",
      "required": ["task", "op"],
      "properties": {
        "task": {
          "type": "string",
          "minLength": 1,
          "description": "Producer task id (capture_output: true)"
        },
        "path": {
          "type": "array",
          "items": { "type": "string", "minLength": 1 },
          "default": [],
          "description": "Path into producer output (e.g. exit_code, stdout)"
        },
        "op": {
          "type": "string",
          "enum": ["eq", "ne", "gt", "lt", "ge", "le", "exists"]
        },
        "value": {
          "description": "Comparison value; omit when op is exists"
        }
      }
    },
    "function": {
      "type": "object",
      "required": ["name"],
      "properties": {
        "name": {
          "enum": [
            "cli_command",
            "command",
            "user_input",
            "git_action",
            "s_e_e_action",
            "foreach",
            "custom",
            "planning_manifest",
            "planning_suite"
          ]
        },
        "input": { "type": "object" }
      }
    }
  }
}
```

See the [workflow authoring guide](/authoring/workflows/) and the
[catalog schema](/schema/catalog/).

Stored definition envelope (hub object; `version` is an integer):
[workflow-definition.schema.json](https://garunski.github.io/s_e_e_library/schema/workflow-definition.schema.json)

Engine content schema (the object in `content`):
[workflow-engine.schema.json](https://garunski.github.io/s_e_e_library/schema/workflow-engine.schema.json)

# Prompt schema

Source: /schema/prompt/

## Prompt homes and references

Choose This machine or Project: Example before creating a prompt. Project files remain under the project's `.s_e_e/prompts/`; machine files are under `~/.s_e_e/definitions/prompts/`. Duplicate ids do not shadow one another. Use `{{prompt.machine:review}}` and `{{prompt.project:review}}` explicitly; bare ids remain project-only. Machine-owned prompts may reference only machine prompts. Missing saved references remain visible for repair.

The picker inserts the canonical reference and opens the chosen home's editor/history. Copy preview shows dependency renames and rewrites. Saving a shared machine prompt affects future uses across projects; delete requires a current usage check. Already captured run content survives source edits/deletion.

MCP named tools and item actions accept qualified ids; omitted scope with a bare id stays project-only, qualified ids infer their home, and disagreeing explicit scope is rejected. Writes require the current conflict token. Project prompt create/update/history/revert use `/api/projects/{code}/definitions/prompts`; machine definitions use `/api/machine/definitions/prompts`. Machine read/edit grants are separate from project access, default off, and edit implies read. Machine MCP advertisements use `machine.<assignment>` and get/completion require an explicit authorized project. Legacy project slug collisions remain explicit rather than ambiguous.

Category `prompt`. Payload file `prompt.json`. Installs to
`.s_e_e/prompts/{file}.json`.

- `id` - prompt id used by `{{prompt.ID}}`. Required, non-empty; may carry a namespace prefix.
- `name` - display name. Required, non-empty.
- `content` - prompt body; a single string (use `\n` for line breaks).
- `created_at` - ISO-8601 timestamp. Optional.

A payload that contains `tasks` is treated as a workflow, not a prompt.

## JSON Schema

Download: [prompt.schema.json](https://garunski.github.io/s_e_e_library/schema/prompt.schema.json)

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "$id": "https://garunski.github.io/s_e_e_library/schema/prompt.schema.json",
  "title": "Prompt package payload (prompt.json)",
  "type": "object",
  "required": ["id", "name"],
  "not": { "required": ["tasks"] },
  "properties": {
    "id": { "type": "string", "minLength": 1 },
    "name": { "type": "string", "minLength": 1 },
    "content": { "type": "string" },
    "created_at": { "type": "string", "format": "date-time" }
  }
}
```

See the [prompt authoring guide](/authoring/prompts/) and the
[catalog schema](/schema/catalog/).

---

# Skill schema

Source: /schema/skill/

Category `skill`. Payload file `SKILL.md`. Installs to
`.agents/skills/{slug}/SKILL.md`.

`SKILL.md` is YAML frontmatter plus a markdown body. Frontmatter:

- `name` - non-empty skill name.
- `description` - non-empty activation description an agent matches against.

The markdown after the frontmatter is the skill instructions.

## JSON Schema

The payload is a markdown file; this schema describes its YAML frontmatter
block. Download: [skill-frontmatter.schema.json](https://garunski.github.io/s_e_e_library/schema/skill-frontmatter.schema.json)

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "$id": "https://garunski.github.io/s_e_e_library/schema/skill-frontmatter.schema.json",
  "title": "Skill SKILL.md YAML frontmatter",
  "type": "object",
  "required": ["name", "description"],
  "properties": {
    "name": { "type": "string", "minLength": 1 },
    "description": { "type": "string", "minLength": 1 }
  }
}
```

See the [skill authoring guide](/authoring/skills/) and the
[catalog schema](/schema/catalog/).

# Command schema

Source: /schema/command/

## Command homes and bindings

Choose This machine or Project: Example before creating a command. Project files remain under the project's `.s_e_e/commands/`; machine files are under `~/.s_e_e/definitions/commands/`. Use `machine:runner` or `project:runner` in workflow defaults, tasks, schedules and cycle stages. Bare ids remain project-only. Same-id commands remain separate; missing or CLI-incompatible choices stay flagged without substitution.

Machine commands can use only machine prompt dependencies. Copy preview identifies dependency rewrites and destination paths before applying. Machine edits affect future uses across projects; current usage and stale previews can block deletion. Authentication settings and server secrets remain application settings rather than definition metadata.

Project command create/update/history/revert use `/api/projects/{code}/definitions/commands`; machine definitions use `/api/machine/definitions/commands`. Reads and writes preserve the selected home; writes require its current conflict token. MCP qualified ids infer scope, while an explicit disagreeing scope is rejected. Machine read/edit grants are independent of project access.

Category `command`. Payload file `command.json`. Installs to
`.s_e_e/commands/{id}.json` (the `to` path must equal this exactly).

- `id` - unique command id; also the install filename. Required, non-empty.
- `name`, `icon` - display metadata.
- `binary` - executable to run. Required, non-empty.
- `base_args` - args always passed.
- `forced_args` - args the engine appends; operators cannot override them.
- `workspace_arg` - `{ flag, value }` for passing the working directory.
- `prompt` - prompt delivery (e.g. `{ "delivery": "stdin" }`).
- `params[]` - typed parameters; each has `key`, `type`, optional `default`, and `map.target` (`env`, `timeout`, `args_append`, `lock_policy`, `stream_toggle`).
- `env` - static environment variables.
- `result` - `success_when` plus `capture[]`.
- `execution` - `cwd` (`spoke`/`hub`), `lock`, `stream`, `non_interactive`.
- `mcp` - optional MCP provisioning. `{ enabled, mechanism? }`. When `enabled` is true and `mechanism` is omitted, delivery defaults to `env`. Mechanisms:
  - `{ "type": "env" }` - inject `SEE_MCP_*` and `MCP_CONFIG`.
  - `{ "type": "config_file", "path": ".cursor/mcp.json", "format": "mcp_servers" }` - write workspace-relative config (restored after the run).
  - `{ "type": "arg", "flag": "--mcp-config", "format": "mcp_servers" }` - pass a temp config file via argv.

A payload with `content` but no `binary` is treated as a prompt.

## JSON Schema

Download: [command.schema.json](https://garunski.github.io/s_e_e_library/schema/command.schema.json)

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "$id": "https://garunski.github.io/s_e_e_library/schema/command.schema.json",
  "title": "Command package payload (command.json)",
  "type": "object",
  "required": ["id", "binary"],
  "properties": {
    "id": { "type": "string", "minLength": 1 },
    "name": { "type": "string" },
    "icon": { "type": "string" },
    "binary": { "type": "string", "minLength": 1 },
    "base_args": { "type": "array", "items": { "type": "string" } },
    "forced_args": { "type": "array", "items": { "type": "string" } },
    "workspace_arg": {
      "type": "object",
      "properties": {
        "flag": { "type": "string" },
        "value": { "type": "string" }
      }
    },
    "prompt": {
      "type": "object",
      "properties": { "delivery": { "type": "string" } }
    },
    "params": {
      "type": "array",
      "items": { "$ref": "#/$defs/param" }
    },
    "env": {
      "type": "object",
      "additionalProperties": { "type": "string" }
    },
    "result": {
      "type": "object",
      "properties": {
        "success_when": { "type": "string" },
        "capture": { "type": "array", "items": { "type": "string" } }
      }
    },
    "execution": {
      "type": "object",
      "properties": {
        "cwd": { "enum": ["spoke", "hub"] },
        "lock": { "type": "object" },
        "stream": { "type": "object" },
        "non_interactive": { "type": "boolean" }
      }
    },
    "mcp": {
      "type": "object",
      "properties": {
        "enabled": { "type": "boolean" },
        "mechanism": { "$ref": "#/$defs/mcpMechanism" }
      }
    }
  },
  "$defs": {
    "mcpMechanism": {
      "type": "object",
      "required": ["type"],
      "properties": {
        "type": { "enum": ["env", "config_file", "arg"] },
        "path": { "type": "string" },
        "flag": { "type": "string" },
        "format": { "type": "string", "enum": ["mcp_servers"] }
      }
    },
    "param": {
      "type": "object",
      "required": ["key"],
      "properties": {
        "key": { "type": "string", "minLength": 1 },
        "type": { "type": "string" },
        "default": {},
        "map": {
          "type": "object",
          "required": ["target"],
          "properties": {
            "target": {
              "enum": ["env", "timeout", "args_append", "lock_policy", "stream_toggle"]
            },
            "name": { "type": "string" }
          }
        }
      }
    }
  }
}
```

See the [command authoring guide](/authoring/commands/) and the
[catalog schema](/schema/catalog/).

# Rule and template schema

Source: /schema/rule-template/

Two lightweight, file-only categories.

## Rule

Category `rule`. Payload is a Cursor rule `.mdc` file (markdown with rule
frontmatter). Installs to `.cursor/rules/{slug}.mdc`.

## Template

Category `template`. Payload is an arbitrary scaffold file. Installs under
`templates/`.

See the [catalog schema](/schema/catalog/) for the manifest and install-path rules.

# Bundle schema

Source: /schema/bundle/

## Library destinations

This machine is available only when the complete package/dependency/member closure contains prompts, commands, workflows or definition-only bundles. A mixed bundle containing a skill, starter, cycle, schedule, rule set or knowledge document is project-only. Preview the concrete destination before installing. Project: Example keeps existing `.s_e_e/` package paths; This machine maps definition files into `~/.s_e_e/definitions/` and keeps independent installed state there. Package metadata and old project installations remain compatible; startup does not migrate or seed machine definitions.

Package workflow `spoke_root` values are removed with a visible preview when copying into the machine home. Direct machine workflow saves must omit `spoke_root`. Dependencies are rewritten to machine references; explicitly review reuse or renamed definitions. Copy/install leaves the source and existing bindings intact.

The same package can be installed independently in both homes. Update/uninstall retains the reviewed home even after project switching. Local edits require acknowledgement; usage, inaccessible projects and stale previews can block removal. Project backups do not contain machine definitions: back up `~/.s_e_e/definitions/` separately. Runs, logs, schedules, cycles and execution history remain project-owned.

Category `bundle`. No payload of its own.

A bundle's catalog `files[]` array installs the payloads of several other
packages together; the build infers each file's kind from its `to` prefix (see
[Install paths](/schema/catalog/#install-paths)).

Bundle metadata lives in its `s_e_e_package.json`:

- `id` - bundle id (e.g. `bundle-author-story`).
- `slug` - url/file-safe slug.
- `category` - `bundle`.
- `name` - display name.
- `description` - one-line summary.
- `labels` - string array.
- `dependencies` - string array of the package `id`s it pulls in.

## JSON Schema

Schema for a bundle's `s_e_e_package.json`. Download:
[bundle-package.schema.json](https://garunski.github.io/s_e_e_library/schema/bundle-package.schema.json)

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "$id": "https://garunski.github.io/s_e_e_library/schema/bundle-package.schema.json",
  "title": "Bundle metadata (s_e_e_package.json)",
  "type": "object",
  "required": ["id", "slug", "category", "name"],
  "properties": {
    "id": { "type": "string", "minLength": 1 },
    "slug": { "type": "string", "minLength": 1 },
    "category": { "const": "bundle" },
    "name": { "type": "string", "minLength": 1 },
    "description": { "type": "string" },
    "labels": { "type": "array", "items": { "type": "string", "minLength": 1 } },
    "dependencies": { "type": "array", "items": { "type": "string", "minLength": 1 } }
  }
}
```

The bundle's `files[]` entries follow the `file` definition in the
[catalog schema](/schema/catalog/#json-schema).

See the [bundle authoring guide](/authoring/bundles/) and the
[catalog schema](/schema/catalog/).

# Cycle schema

Source: /schema/cycle/

Category `cycle`. Payload file `cycle.json`. Installs to
`.s_e_e/cycles/{id}.json` (the `to` path must equal `.s_e_e/cycles/` plus the
document `id` plus `.json`).

- `id` - stable cycle id; must match the install file name.
- `name` - display name.
- `host` - `orchestrator` or `knowledge` (the hosts the app can activate today).
- `schema_version` - integer, currently `1`.
- `stores` - store keys this cycle uses; each must be declared for that host in
  the app registry.
- `stages[]` - each stage has `key`, `verb`, `workflow_definition_id`,
  `trigger` (`tick`, `schedule`, `event`, or `manual`), `reads`, and `writes`.

See the [cycle authoring guide](/authoring/cycles/) for store registry keys,
the gate stage on the orchestrator host, and activation checks.

## JSON Schema

Download: [cycle-document.schema.json](https://garunski.github.io/s_e_e_library/schema/cycle-document.schema.json)

```json
{
  "$schema": "http://json-schema.org/draft-07/schema#",
  "$id": "https://see.local/schema/cycle-document",
  "title": "Cycle document",
  "type": "object",
  "required": ["id", "name", "host", "schema_version", "stores", "stages"],
  "additionalProperties": false,
  "properties": {
    "id": {
      "type": "string",
      "minLength": 1
    },
    "name": {
      "type": "string",
      "minLength": 1
    },
    "host": {
      "type": "string",
      "enum": ["orchestrator", "knowledge", "stories", "events"]
    },
    "schema_version": {
      "type": "integer",
      "minimum": 1
    },
    "stores": {
      "type": "array",
      "items": { "type": "string", "minLength": 1 },
      "uniqueItems": true
    },
    "stages": {
      "type": "array",
      "minItems": 1,
      "items": {
        "type": "object",
        "required": [
          "key",
          "verb",
          "workflow_definition_id",
          "trigger",
          "reads",
          "writes"
        ],
        "additionalProperties": false,
        "properties": {
          "key": { "type": "string", "minLength": 1 },
          "verb": { "type": "string", "minLength": 1 },
          "workflow_definition_id": { "type": "string", "minLength": 1 },
          "trigger": {
            "type": "string",
            "enum": ["tick", "schedule", "event", "manual"]
          },
          "reads": {
            "type": "array",
            "items": { "type": "string", "minLength": 1 }
          },
          "writes": { "type": "string", "minLength": 1 }
        }
      }
    }
  }
}
```

See the [catalog schema](/schema/catalog/).

# Hub config schema

Source: /schema/hub-config/

Project settings > Experimental manages `project.experimental_features`. Its six boolean keys are `orchestrator`, `orchestrator_cycle`, `knowledge_cycle`, `planning_cycle`, `knowledge_research` and `global_chat`. Existing and new projects resolve missing objects or keys to false without an eager migration write. Unknown experiment keys and non-boolean values are rejected. Only `orchestrator_cycle` depends on its configured parent `orchestrator`. Other switches, including Global Chat, are independent.

`GET /api/projects/{project}/experimental-features` returns `configured`, `effective` and `conflict_token`. `PATCH` on that path accepts `{"changes":{"global_chat":true},"conflict_token":"latest-read-token"}`. Send only changed boolean keys. Stale tokens return HTTP 409 without mutation. Use the canonical successful response for subsequent writes. Effective values and tokens are response fields. Stored configuration contains configured booleans only.

Disabling preserves data, schedules and saved run controls and does not cancel admitted work. Fresh admission stops. Subsequent feature-owned HTTP and MCP calls, including calls from existing runs, fail explicitly with `EXPERIMENTAL_FEATURE_DISABLED`. Generic execution, process, log and stop controls remain available. Enabling may resume scheduling on the next normal tick. Manual stories, milestones, shared objectives, knowledge docs and decisions, reusable workflows and Library package storage remain available. Providers, models, routing, spend, `/v1/chat/completions` and workflow-space defaults remain available.

MCP tool discovery is the union across authorized projects, restricted to the bound project when present. A mixed-project client can see a tool enabled elsewhere. Every invocation checks the target project afresh. Exact-project resources and qualified Research prompts follow target availability. Clients supporting list-change notifications refresh discovery after changes. Cached tool lists do not authorize calls.

Hub data-root `config.json`. Must be a non-empty JSON object.

- `project` - object; typically includes `id`.
- `overrides` - object.
- `library` - catalog sources and collections. See [catalog schema](/schema/catalog/).
- `stories` - see [stories config](/schema/stories-config/).
- `llm.routing` - see [routing rules](/schema/routing-rules/).
- `orchestrator` - see [orchestrator policy](/schema/orchestrator-policy/).

Unknown top-level keys are kept.

## Conditional project settings writes

Project settings writes accept an optional expected_settings object containing the last-read values for the edited section. The expected_settings fields on PUT /api/projects/{project} are name, hub_path, and command_timeout_secs (null means no override). On PUT /api/projects/{project}/command-defaults they are default_command_id (null means none) and default_workflow_by_command. The patch still uses clear_command_timeout:true or clear_default_command:true to remove the respective override. Comparison and patch run together under the server write coordinator; stale values return HTTP 409 without mutation. Omission preserves existing unconditional callers. For example, send {"name":"New name","expected_settings":{"name":"Old name"}}. Use current values from the latest project read or successful write; hub_path corresponds to the project response path field. Timeout updates persist in hub config and preserve other sections.

## JSON Schema

Download: [hub-config.schema.json](https://garunski.github.io/s_e_e_library/schema/hub-config.schema.json)

```json
{
  "$schema": "http://json-schema.org/draft-07/schema#",
  "$id": "https://garunski.github.io/s_e_e_library/schema/hub-config.schema.json",
  "title": "Hub config.json",
  "type": "object",
  "minProperties": 1,
  "additionalProperties": true,
  "properties": {
    "project": {
      "type": "object",
      "additionalProperties": true,
      "properties": {
        "experimental_features": {
          "type": "object",
          "additionalProperties": false,
          "properties": {
            "orchestrator": {
              "type": "boolean",
              "default": false
            },
            "orchestrator_cycle": {
              "type": "boolean",
              "default": false
            },
            "knowledge_cycle": {
              "type": "boolean",
              "default": false
            },
            "planning_cycle": {
              "type": "boolean",
              "default": false
            },
            "knowledge_research": {
              "type": "boolean",
              "default": false
            },
            "global_chat": {
              "type": "boolean",
              "default": false
            }
          }
        },
        "id": {
          "type": "string"
        },
        "admin_spoke": {
          "type": "string"
        },
        "spokes": {
          "type": "array",
          "items": {
            "type": "object",
            "required": [
              "name",
              "path"
            ],
            "properties": {
              "name": {
                "type": "string"
              },
              "path": {
                "type": "string"
              },
              "labels": {
                "type": "array",
                "items": {
                  "type": "string"
                }
              }
            }
          }
        },
        "default_command_id": {
          "type": "string"
        },
        "default_workflow_by_command": {
          "type": "object",
          "additionalProperties": {
            "type": "string"
          }
        }
      }
    },
    "overrides": {
      "type": "object"
    },
    "stories": {
      "type": "object"
    },
    "library": {
      "type": "object"
    },
    "llm": {
      "type": "object"
    },
    "knowledge": {
      "type": "object",
      "additionalProperties": true,
      "properties": {
        "cycle_enabled": {
          "type": "boolean"
        }
      }
    },
    "orchestrator": {
      "type": "object"
    }
  }
}
```

# App settings schema

Source: /schema/app-settings/

## Definition storage and grants

Machine definitions belong to the current OS user under `~/.s_e_e/definitions/`, separately from application settings and secrets in `~/.s_e_e/settings.json`. Back up that definition directory separately from project backups and Git. Client grants default machine definition read/edit off; edit implies read. Project authorization is separate. Runs, logs, schedules, cycles and execution history remain per project.

User-level `~/.s_e_e/settings.json`.

- `theme` - `light`, `dark`, or `system`.
- `notifications`, `auth_enabled`, `mcp_enabled`, `llm_content_capture_enabled` - booleans.
- `editor_auto_save` - boolean, default false. Reserved for the editor autosave rollout; the switch is not exposed yet. Legacy `auto_save` is ignored. Settings PUTs omitting `editor_auto_save` preserve its saved value.
- `default_workflow` - string or null.
- `server_url`, `api_port`, `cors_origins` - strings.
- `audit_retention_hours`, `log_retention_hours`, `session_ttl_hours`, `command_timeout_secs` - integer or null.
- `schedule_retention` - object.
- `log_stream_retention` - per-stream retention days. Null keeps a stream indefinitely.
- `diagnostic_logging` - diagnostic JSON capture policy, defaulting to Info with no category overrides.
- `command_binary_allowlist` - string array.
- `command_secrets` - string map.

## Diagnostic logging

Settings > Retention > Logging edits `diagnostic_logging`. Stored `default_level` and `overrides` values are `trace`, `debug`, `info`, `warn`, `error` or `off`. Overrides accept `server`, `trace`, `timing` and `frontend`. Each threshold captures its level and higher. Off suppresses every diagnostic level in that category. Inherit removes the category key.

```json
{
  "diagnostic_logging": {
    "default_level": "info",
    "overrides": {"server": "debug", "trace": "off"}
  }
}
```

This fragment captures server Debug diagnostics, suppresses trace diagnostics and leaves timing/frontend at Info. Missing policy defaults to Info with no overrides. An API update omitting the policy preserves its previous value. Supplying it replaces the whole policy. An empty object resets it to defaults, and empty overrides restores category inheritance.

Saved policy applies immediately to subsequent server writes. Workers keep their launch snapshot, and newly launched workers receive updates. `RUST_LOG` independently controls ordinary tracing. Viewer filters select stored entries. Verbosity changes leave historical files intact, while retention determines file expiry.

Audit, process lifecycle and raw output, workflow history and LLM accounting remain captured at diagnostic Off under their independent capture and retention policies. Raw stdout and stderr use Trace with `severity_origin=raw_capture` and separate source labels. Successful polling/search diagnostics are Debug, meaningful changes are Info, recoverable failures are Warn and terminal failures are Error.

Stream retention defaults in days are `audit_days=365`, `llm_days=365`, `server_days=30`, `trace_days=30` (also timing), `workflow_days=30`, `frontend_days=30`, `process_days=14` and `entity_change_meta_days=90`. A null value retains that stream indefinitely. Stream values take precedence over `log_retention_hours`, whose fallback is 48 hours. The legacy `audit_retention_hours` field does not control stream expiry.

## JSON Schema

Download: [app-settings.schema.json](https://garunski.github.io/s_e_e_library/schema/app-settings.schema.json)

```json
{
  "$schema": "http://json-schema.org/draft-07/schema#",
  "$id": "https://garunski.github.io/s_e_e_library/schema/app-settings.schema.json",
  "title": "App settings.json",
  "type": "object",
  "additionalProperties": true,
  "definitions": {
    "diagnostic_threshold": { "enum": ["trace", "debug", "info", "warn", "error", "off"] }
  },
  "properties": {
    "theme": { "enum": ["light", "dark", "system"] },
    "notifications": { "type": "boolean" },
    "editor_auto_save": { "type": "boolean", "default": false },
    "default_workflow": { "type": ["string", "null"] },
    "server_url": { "type": "string" },
    "api_port": { "type": "string" },
    "cors_origins": { "type": "string" },
    "audit_retention_hours": { "type": ["integer", "null"], "minimum": 0 },
    "log_retention_hours": { "type": ["integer", "null"], "minimum": 0 },
    "auth_enabled": { "type": "boolean" },
    "session_ttl_hours": { "type": ["integer", "null"], "minimum": 0 },
    "schedule_retention": { "type": "object" },
    "log_stream_retention": { "type": "object" },
    "diagnostic_logging": {
      "type": "object",
      "additionalProperties": false,
      "properties": {
        "default_level": { "$ref": "#/definitions/diagnostic_threshold" },
        "overrides": {
          "type": "object",
          "additionalProperties": false,
          "properties": {
            "server": { "$ref": "#/definitions/diagnostic_threshold" },
            "trace": { "$ref": "#/definitions/diagnostic_threshold" },
            "timing": { "$ref": "#/definitions/diagnostic_threshold" },
            "frontend": { "$ref": "#/definitions/diagnostic_threshold" }
          }
        }
      }
    },
    "command_timeout_secs": { "type": ["integer", "null"], "minimum": 0 },
    "command_binary_allowlist": { "type": "array", "items": { "type": "string" } },
    "command_secrets": { "type": "object", "additionalProperties": { "type": "string" } },
    "mcp_enabled": { "type": "boolean" },
    "llm_content_capture_enabled": { "type": "boolean" }
  }
}
```

# Routing rules schema

Source: /schema/routing-rules/

LLM routing rules. Stored as `llm.routing` in [hub config](/schema/hub-config/).

- `task_profiles` - required object. Each value is `{ provider, model, requires_tool_calling? }`. `provider` and `model` are required.
- `cost_caps` - object. Each value is `{ max_usd }`.

At least one task profile is required at save time.

## JSON Schema

Download: [routing-rules.schema.json](https://garunski.github.io/s_e_e_library/schema/routing-rules.schema.json)

```json
{
  "$schema": "http://json-schema.org/draft-07/schema#",
  "$id": "https://garunski.github.io/s_e_e_library/schema/routing-rules.schema.json",
  "title": "LLM routing rules",
  "type": "object",
  "required": ["task_profiles"],
  "additionalProperties": true,
  "properties": {
    "task_profiles": {
      "type": "object",
      "additionalProperties": {
        "type": "object",
        "required": ["provider", "model"],
        "additionalProperties": true,
        "properties": {
          "provider": { "type": "string", "minLength": 1 },
          "model": { "type": "string" },
          "requires_tool_calling": { "type": "boolean" }
        }
      }
    },
    "cost_caps": {
      "type": "object",
      "additionalProperties": {
        "type": "object",
        "required": ["max_usd"],
        "properties": { "max_usd": { "type": "number" } }
      }
    }
  }
}
```

# Stories config schema

Source: /schema/stories-config/

Stories section of [hub config](/schema/hub-config/).

- `project_name` - required, non-empty.
- `statuses` - string array.
- `labels` - string array.
- `date_format` - non-empty string when present.
- `default_create_status` - string.

## JSON Schema

Download: [stories-config.schema.json](https://garunski.github.io/s_e_e_library/schema/stories-config.schema.json)

```json
{

  "type": "object",

  "additionalProperties": true,

    "project_name": { "type": "string", "minLength": 1 },
    "statuses": { "type": "array", "items": { "type": "string", "minLength": 1 } },
    "labels": { "type": "array", "items": { "type": "string" } },
    "date_format": { "type": "string", "minLength": 1 },
    "default_create_status": { "type": "string" }
  }
}
```

# Orchestrator policy schema

Source: /schema/orchestrator-policy/

Orchestrator policy. Stored as `orchestrator` in [hub config](/schema/hub-config/).

- `auto_mode` - `off`, `assisted`, or `auto`.
- `policy` - required. `levels` maps action classes to `auto`, `propose`, or `forbid`.
- `budgets` - required object (run caps, spend caps, window).

GET and PUT `/api/projects/{project}/orchestrator/policy` return a section `conflict_token`. Pass the last returned token on PUT to reject stale edits with HTTP 409. Omitting the token preserves legacy unconditional updates. Omitting `auto_mode` preserves the current mode. Writes preserve other hub configuration sections and do not start a run.

## JSON Schema

Download: [orchestrator-policy.schema.json](https://garunski.github.io/s_e_e_library/schema/orchestrator-policy.schema.json)

```json
{
  "$schema": "http://json-schema.org/draft-07/schema#",
  "$id": "https://garunski.github.io/s_e_e_library/schema/orchestrator-policy.schema.json",
  "title": "Orchestrator policy document",
  "type": "object",
  "required": ["policy", "budgets"],
  "additionalProperties": true,
  "properties": {
    "auto_mode": { "enum": ["off", "assisted", "auto"] },
    "policy": {
      "type": "object",
      "additionalProperties": true,
      "properties": {
        "levels": {
          "type": "object",
          "additionalProperties": { "enum": ["auto", "propose", "forbid"] }
        }
      }
    },
    "budgets": { "type": "object" }
  }
}
```

---

# Schedule schema

Source: /schema/schedule/

Workflow schedule. Installs to `.s_e_e/workflows/schedules/{id}.json`. Bundles may include schedule files; kind is inferred from the `to` prefix.

- `id`, `name`, `workflow_id` - required, non-empty.
- `kind` - required object with a `kind` tag (`cron`, `interval`, or `entity_event`).
- `enabled` - required boolean.
- `concurrency`, `runtime_inputs`, `story_rules`, `catchup_policy`, `notifications` - objects.

Subject filters can point at a [rule set](/schema/schedule-rule-set/) by id.

## Conditional HTTP updates

`PUT /api/projects/{project}/workflow-schedules/{id}` accepts `{ "schedule": { ... }, "expected_updated_at": "2026-11-08T00:00:00Z" }`. Use the `updated_at` returned by the latest read or successful write. The comparison and replacement are serialized with schedule writes. A stale revision or deleted record returns HTTP 409 without mutation. Omitting `expected_updated_at` preserves unconditional upsert behavior.

```json
{
  "schedule": {
    "id": "nightly",
    "name": "Nightly",
    "workflow_id": "project:quality",
    "kind": { "kind": "interval", "every_seconds": 3600 },
    "enabled": false,
    "created_at": "2026-11-08T00:00:00Z",
    "updated_at": "2026-11-08T00:00:00Z"
  },
  "expected_updated_at": "2026-11-08T00:00:00Z"
}
```

## JSON Schema

Download: [schedule.schema.json](https://garunski.github.io/s_e_e_library/schema/schedule.schema.json)

```json
{
  "$schema": "http://json-schema.org/draft-07/schema#",
  "$id": "https://garunski.github.io/s_e_e_library/schema/schedule.schema.json",
  "title": "Workflow schedule",
  "type": "object",
  "required": ["id", "name", "workflow_id", "kind", "enabled"],
  "additionalProperties": true,
  "properties": {
    "id": { "type": "string", "minLength": 1 },
    "name": { "type": "string", "minLength": 1 },
    "workflow_id": { "type": "string", "minLength": 1 },
    "kind": { "type": "object", "required": ["kind"] },
    "enabled": { "type": "boolean" },
    "concurrency": { "type": "object" },
    "runtime_inputs": { "type": "object" },
    "story_rules": { "type": "object" },
    "catchup_policy": { "type": "object" },
    "notifications": { "type": "object" }
  }
}
```

# Schedule rule set schema

Source: /schema/schedule-rule-set/

Schedule rule set. Installs to `.s_e_e/workflows/schedule_rule_sets/{id}.json`.

- `id`, `name` - required, non-empty.
- `description` - string.
- `rules` - object (statuses, labels, acceptance-criteria flags).

See [schedule](/schema/schedule/) for `story_rules` that point at a rule set id.

## Conditional HTTP updates

PUT /api/projects/{project}/workflow-schedule-rule-sets/{id} accepts the rule set fields and an optional expected_updated_at timestamp from the last GET or successful save. For example, add `"expected_updated_at": "2026-11-08T00:00:01Z"` beside id and name. The comparison and write are serialized. A stale timestamp or deleted record returns HTTP 409 without changing the record. Omitting the field preserves unconditional upsert behavior. Successful saves return the stored rule set and its new updated_at; expected_updated_at is request-only and is not stored.

## JSON Schema

Download: [schedule-rule-set.schema.json](https://garunski.github.io/s_e_e_library/schema/schedule-rule-set.schema.json)

```json
{
  "$schema": "http://json-schema.org/draft-07/schema#",
  "$id": "https://garunski.github.io/s_e_e_library/schema/schedule-rule-set.schema.json",
  "title": "Schedule rule set",
  "type": "object",
  "required": ["id", "name"],
  "additionalProperties": true,
  "properties": {
    "id": { "type": "string", "minLength": 1 },
    "name": { "type": "string", "minLength": 1 },
    "description": { "type": "string" },
    "rules": { "type": "object" }
  }
}
```
